title: chard measurement report
description: One report = one (environment x toolchain x profile) measured by the full probe set. Reports are append-only facts; comparison tables are derived by joining reports. The column key of that join is the tuple (environment.distro.id, environment.distro.version_id, toolchain.id, profile.id), and the row key is observations[].check; observations[].flag is the row's display spelling, and the check id is the only key. profile.id carries a digest of the flag lists for an explicit profile, so two explicit runs with different lists are two columns. run.id is a digest of the measurement itself, taken over run.inputs_sha256 and every check's verdict and level (run.inputs_sha256 names the inputs it covers), and identifies a measurement rather than an invocation: two identical measurements share it, and two columns never do. There is no alias map for renamed row keys; a check id that changes needs one here.

chard_schema.description: The major version of this document's shape. When it moves is the CLI contract's rule (`chard --help`; DESIGN.md, "The command-line contract"): a key chard adds is not a change, which is why every object here admits one. The predicate language's definitions under `$defs`, copied from `schema/chard-predicate.schema.json`, stay closed: an evaluator refuses a predicate key it does not know rather than ignore it.

id.description: Sixteen hex digits of a SHA-256 over `inputs=<run.inputs_sha256>` and then each observation's check, verdict and level, sorted, one `cell=` line each. It identifies a column of the join measured to one outcome: two identical measurements share an id, two that differ in any input or any verdict do not, and the clock is not an input. The `run-id-disagrees-with-measurement` consistency rule recomputes it from the report.

inputs_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 over what the run was asked to measure, before any result, as canonical `key=value` lines in this order: chard_schema; run.harness_version; run.harness_revision (`unknown` when absent); run.harness_revision_source and run.harness_rustflags_sha256, each only when present, so an absent one adds no line; run.probe_corpus_sha256; run.deadlines; the check selection, the observations' checks and coverage.checks_missing less coverage.checks_unexpected, sorted; whether structured diagnostics were requested; profile.id, flags_source, cflags, cxxflags and ldflags; toolchain.id, kind, version_raw, target_triple, driver, cxx_driver, configure_args, config_files and predefined_macros_sha256; toolchain.linker's kind, version, path and profile_flags, and the same four of linker.cxx; environment.distro.id and version_id; environment.libc.impl and version; environment.kernel.release and arch; environment.cpu.vendor and relevant_features; environment.execution.mode, mode_evidence.basis and image; image_attestation.status and digest; and, only when image_attestation.installed_disk is present, its sha256, installed_at and installed_from_digest, so a report without one adds none of their lines. An absent value is the bare key, lists are joined by U+001F, and a backslash or newline in a value is escaped. The clock, the invocation, prose, derived fields (kernel.is_host_kernel, kernel.ownership, linker.artifact), run.decoders_sha256 (which run.probe_corpus_sha256 carries), evidence_filters, --emit-macros and every result are left out, so two runs asked the same thing share it whatever they found. The `run-id-disagrees-with-measurement` consistency rule recomputes it.

duration_ms.x-volatile: Wall-clock time of the whole run. 0 under --normalize.

harness_revision.description: VCS revision of the harness, if known.

harness_revision_source.description: Which source named run.harness_revision: read from the tree the harness compiled (`git`; `archive`, the `REVISION` file a `git archive` fills in; `cargo-vcs`, a crate archive's `.cargo_vcs_info.json`), or `asserted` by `CHARD_REVISION` at build time, which nothing checks against the tree. An asserted revision joins only reports asserted alike. Absent exactly where run.harness_revision is.

harness_rustflags_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 of the rustflags cargo built the harness under, as cargo hands them to the build script (`CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`: the flags separated by U+001F, from `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS` or a config file's rustflags). A report carrying one joins only reports built under the same flags. Absent where cargo passed none.

probe_corpus_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 over the self-report header, run.decoders_sha256, and every probe and check the corpus holds, each through an exhaustive destructure of its fields: every probe's language, link mode, source and link libraries, and every check's flag, channel, polarity, confidence, observable, level scale and ask, controls, gate, the tables a cut withholds on, and its decoder (a predicate in its canonical form, or the kind `code` and the name of the detector function the check names). Prose (titles, notes, defects, references) is left out. Two reports carrying one value were produced by one corpus read by one set of decoders; `table`, `matrix` and `dataset` refuse to mix values.

decoders_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the fingerprint over the code that turned this run's evidence into readings, as `chard probes` publishes it under `decoders_sha256`. The SHA-256 over the predicate language version (`chard-predicate/1`), each macro and elf-static check's id and predicate in canonical form in corpus order, and the source of every file under src/predicate/ and src/decode/ other than the `*_tests.rs` unit-test files beside them, and of src/elf.rs, each read up to its top-level `#[cfg(test)]` with comment lines and blank lines dropped (the list is `probe::DECODER_SOURCES`, which `tests/decode_layout.rs` holds to the tree); every part is framed by its length. Folded into run.probe_corpus_sha256, and published on its own so a reader comparing two reports whose corpus hashes differ can tell whether the decoders did. Which code decoder a runtime or compiler-diag check names is bound by run.probe_corpus_sha256, through the detector's name.

invocation.description: argv of the harness itself, with argv[0] reduced to the text after its last `/` and every other argument as given, so the values of --workdir, --output, -o and --image-attestation are the paths the operator wrote. An argument that is not UTF-8 has each invalid sequence replaced by U+FFFD. Under --normalize argv[0] reads `chard` and those values read `<normalized>`; every other argument is the measurement's own configuration and stays.
invocation.x-volatile: Names where this run put things. Path-valued options are replaced under --normalize.

deadlines.description: Every deadline that could have shaped a value in this report, in whole milliseconds. A probe still running at `probe_run_ms` is killed and its run record reads `timed_out`; a compiler invocation still running at `compile_ms` is killed and recorded as failed, and `compile_drain_grace_ms` further bounds reading its output once it has exited.

probe_run_ms.description: `--timeout`, applied to each probe run on its own. Every run record's `deadline_ms` carries the same value.

environment.description: Where the measurement happened. Distinct from `toolchain`: the same toolchain measured under a different kernel can give different runtime verdicts.

id.description: os-release ID, e.g. ubuntu, fedora, alpine, arch, debian.

arch.description: The architecture chard's own binary was compiled for (Rust's `std::env::consts::ARCH`), e.g. x86_64, aarch64. While chard runs natively this is the kernel's architecture, the word `uname -m` prints; under qemu-user an aarch64 chard on an x86_64 kernel publishes `aarch64` here. `machine` is the kernel's own word.

machine.description: The kernel's own machine, read from Linux's `/proc/sys/kernel/arch`, which qemu-user does not intercept as it does `uname(2)` and `/proc/cpuinfo`. Absent where the file is absent (every non-Linux platform, and Linux kernels older than the sysctl). Compared with each runtime artifact's `elf.machine` to decide `run-under-emulation`.

is_host_kernel.description: True when environment.execution.mode is container: the kernel is the host's rather than the measured distro's. Derived from the mode alone, so false where the mode is host by default as well as on an asserted host or vm; `ownership` says which. The checks that declare needs_vm are withheld under `needs-vm` when this is true and under `execution-mode-assumed` on the default; every other runtime check is measured either way.

ownership.description: Whose kernel the run's is, derived from environment.execution.mode read with environment.execution.mode_evidence.basis, the attribution the needs_vm gate reads. `own`: the operator asserted `host` or `vm` with `--execution`, so the kernel is taken as the measured system's on that word, which nothing chard reads corroborates (chard observes no mode but `container`); the checks that declare needs_vm are not withheld on this field. `borrowed`: the mode is `container`, observed or asserted, so the kernel is the host's (`is_host_kernel` is true); those checks are withheld under `needs-vm`. `unsettled`: the basis is `assumed-host`, the default (`measure` writes mode `host` there), where nothing chard reads tells a system that owns its kernel from a container it has no instrument for; those checks are withheld under `execution-mode-assumed`, and `is_host_kernel` reads false. No other check is withheld on this field. Held to the mode and basis by `kernel-ownership-disagrees-with-execution-mode`, at publish and on read. Required of what `measure` writes; a report without it is still read by `table` and `matrix`, held on `is_host_kernel` alone, and `matrix` names its cell `unpublished`. How the version moves on a new required key is the schema rule in DESIGN.md.

impl.description: Held against `env::LIBC_NAMES` by tests/schema_conformance.rs, in both directions. It drifted while nothing did: `openbsd` was returnable and undeclared, so the first OpenBSD report would have failed validation, and `uclibc` and `other` were declared and unreachable.

relevant_features.description: Only features that gate a hardening mechanism: ibt, shstk, user_shstk, smap, bti, pauth. A binary can be IBT-marked on a CPU that cannot enforce it.

mode.description: container shares the host kernel; kernel-enforced runtime probes are only valid under vm or host.

detection.description: How the execution mode was determined, recorded so a reader can judge how much to trust it.

image_attestation.description: What established that the system measured is the image this report names. Present unconditionally: an omitted field would read as nothing-to-report when what is being reported is that nothing established the image. chard runs inside the image and cannot verify this from there, so an attestation is recorded as received rather than as a verification chard performed.

status.description: not-applicable when measuring the running system; unattested when an image was named with nothing carried in to support the name; attested when a fetcher's provenance object was supplied. A digest mismatch never appears here: measure refuses to publish.

established_by.description: What the reader is being asked to trust, in words.

verdict.description: The fetcher's own verdict: signature-verified, signed-unpinned, digest-matched, unverified. A digest matching a manifest served over TLS is weaker than a digest under a signature.

served_by.description: Host that served the bytes; a mirror where the publisher uses a redirector.

origin.description: How `url` came to be known, because the three are different strengths of the same field. `recorded-at-fetch` is the VM lane, where the fetcher wrote the URL as it downloaded. `confirmed-by-refetch` is weaker: the publisher was shown to serve byte-identical content at that URL, which does not establish that this copy came from there — used by the container lanes, whose artifacts predate any URL recording and which are verified rather than replaced so no measured row moves. `not-recorded` means the chain stops at a local file. Where it is absent, it reads as `not-recorded`.

manifest_fetched.description: Whether the publisher's manifest was retrieved at all. Distinguishes `the manifest said X and the image is Y` — a statement about the image, which is refused — from `there was no manifest to compare against`, which says nothing about the bytes and yields `unattested`. Where it is absent, it reads as true.

installed_disk.description: Present only when the disk that booted is not the artifact `digest` names but one installed from it, as the harness's Alpine guests are installed from the publisher's signed installer ISO; absent, never null, when the verified artifact is itself what booted. Received from the fetcher's install record rather than verified: chard runs on the installed disk and cannot hash it. Hashed into run.inputs_sha256, so two different installed disks give two different input digests. See `env::InstalledDisk`.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the installed disk image, recorded after the install and re-checked by the fetcher before every boot.

installed_at.description: When the installer started, UTC. For a rolling branch such as Alpine edge this dates every package installed.

installed_from_digest.description: The digest, in `digest_kind`, of the artifact installed from. chard refuses an attestation in which this differs from `digest`.

mode_evidence.description: What chard observed about the execution mode, beside what it was told. `mode` gates whether kernel-enforced verdicts are attributed to the named distribution. Present unconditionally, so that `host` by default is distinguishable from `host` by measurement. The checks that declare `needs_vm` are withheld under `execution-mode-assumed` on the default, and measured on an asserted `host` or `vm`.

basis.description: asserted-and-contradicted never appears: the consistency pass refuses such a report, since it is two claims about one property that disagree.

observed.description: What chard observed. Absent when no instrument settled it, which is not the same as host.

observation.description: The instrument that settled `container` (a runtime's marker file, a cgroup needle, systemd's `/run/systemd/container`, a `container=` word on PID 1, or a user namespace) and what it returned; where none did, what each of the two positive markers read, absent, unreadable (named as such, not as absent, and claiming nothing about presence), empty, or read without the word, as systemd reads its own markers. The user-namespace sentence carries the two markers' readings beside it.

id.description: Stable label used as a join key across reports: kind-version-libc-distro, e.g. "gcc-16.1.1-glibc2.43-fedora44". The libc tag is environment.libc.impl and environment.libc.version run together, or the implementation alone when no version was read; the distribution tag is environment.distro.id and environment.distro.version_id run together, or the id alone when the version is `unknown`. Composed once, after the environment is read, so no report carries a key missing either half.

version_raw.description: Verbatim first line of the driver's --version. Empty where it exited 0 and printed nothing; absent where that job did not exit 0 with its output whole, with a warning diagnostic whose context is `toolchain.version_raw`; kind and version are read from the macro dump either way.

driver.description: Path to the compiler driver actually invoked.

configure_args.description: From `gcc -v`. This is where --enable-default-pie / --enable-default-ssp show up, i.e. the provenance of `bare` defaults.

config_files.description: The configuration files the driver announced loading in `-v`: clang's `Configuration file:` lines (/etc/clang/*.cfg, --config) and gcc's `Reading specs from <path>`, printed when an installed specs file replaces the built-in specs. A real distro-defaults mechanism that is invisible in --version; when the list is non-empty a `bare` column's `profile.flags_source` reads `driver-config-file`.

linker.description: The linker the profile links with, and what the linked artifacts said about that identity; the object is `$defs/linker`.

target.description: The architecture every `arch-gated` decision was taken under, held to four witnesses: the `e_machine` of the ELF artifacts the run built, the architecture macros of the driver's intrinsic macro dump with no flags (`macros`), those of the same dump under the profile's C flags (`profile_macros`), and those of the C++ driver's dump under the profile's C++ flags where they differ (`profile_macros_cxx`). The gate decides before any build, so an arch-gated verdict rests on this premise whichever way it went. Where an artifact carries a machine, or a macro names one, under which a check's gate decides otherwise, that check's observations are withheld as `indeterminate` under `gating.rule: target-arch-contradicted`, and the consistency rule `arch-gate-contradicted-by-artifacts` refuses a report that publishes one of them otherwise. The decision is compared whole (measured, gated out, unread, outside the mechanism table), so a witnessed machine the table has no row for (a dump defining none of the three macros, or an `e_machine` the table has no row for) withholds every arch-gated check, the ones gated out under `arch` included; an `e_machine` of another family the table has a row for withholds the checks whose gate decides otherwise under it. A dump defining none of the three beside artifacts that all carry `arch`'s family, one of them built by a probe of the dump's language, is `overruled` by them and withholds nothing. The width and byte order are held too (`abi`): an artifact of the read family, or a dump that agreed about the family, at a width or order other than the one the architecture's rows stand for (ELF64 little-endian for `x86_64` and `aarch64`, ELF32 little-endian for `x86`: an x32, aarch64 ILP32 or aarch64_be target) is a target the table has no row for, and every arch-gated check is withheld under `gating.rule: target-abi-contradicted`, except one the machine comparison withheld first.

arch.description: The value compared against each check's architecture list: `x86_64`, `x86`, `aarch64`, or the first component of `target_triple` as the driver printed it.

source.description: `dumpmachine`: the first component of the driver's `-dumpmachine` answer (`target_triple`). `kernel`: `environment.kernel.arch`, because `-dumpmachine` gave nothing to parse. `profile-macros`: the one architecture macro `profile_macros` defined, because the profile's C flags select a target (`-m32`, `-m64`, `--target=`, `-target`, `-arch`), which `-dumpmachine`, asked with no flags, cannot see; read only where that dump completed and defined exactly one of the three. The consistency rule `arch-gate-contradicted-by-artifacts` re-derives `arch` and `source` from `target_triple`, `profile_macros` and `environment.kernel.arch`.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every ELF artifact read carries the machine family of `arch`. `disagrees`: an artifact carries another family, or the run's own artifacts carry more than one (a profile flag such as `-m32` does this as surely as a driver whose `-dumpmachine` names another target); published with an error diagnostic under `toolchain.target`. `unmapped`: `arch` names no machine family chard maps, and the artifacts carry one; a warning diagnostic where that machine flips a gate. `no-elf-artifact`: nothing was read (a Mach-O host, or a selection that builds nothing), and `arch` stands uncorroborated.

machines.description: The stored `elf.machine` of the observations' builds to the number of distinct artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, that carry it.

artifacts_read.description: Distinct ELF artifacts read, relocatables included: the compiler's `e_machine` is in a `.o` as in a linked output.

evidence.description: The machines, the first artifact carrying each, where `arch` came from, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: The width and byte order of the artifacts of the read family and of the dumps that agreed about the family, held to the ones the mechanism table's rows for `arch` stand for. Read only from what agrees about the family: an artifact of another `e_machine` or a dump naming another family withholds under the machine comparison already, and an overruled, superseded or failed dump witnesses nothing.

expected.description: The width and order `arch`'s rows stand for, the hosts they were measured on; absent where `arch` has no row in the table.

artifacts.description: Each `ELF<class> <order>` among the artifacts of the read family, to the number of distinct artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, carrying it. A record with no `elf_data` is left out.

dumps.description: Each dump whose agreement about the family is `agrees` and that defined `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__`, by the name the evidence gives it, to the `ELF<class> <order>` those two name.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every artifact and dump read carries `expected`. `disagrees`: one carries another width or order, and every arch-gated check is withheld under `target-abi-contradicted`. `unmapped`: `arch` has no row, so nothing is expected. `no-witness`: no artifact of the family was read and no agreeing dump named a width and order.

evidence.description: What `arch`'s rows stand for, what each witness carried, and why the agreement follows.

macros.description: The second witness: the architecture macros the driver's intrinsic macro dump (`cc -dM -E` with no profile flags, as `-dumpmachine` is asked) defined. It exists on a run that reads no ELF artifact, where `agreement` reads `no-elf-artifact`, and it witnesses the driver's own target: a target the profile's flags select (`-m32`, `--target=`, `-arch x86_64`) agrees with `-dumpmachine` here by construction, and is `profile_macros`'s to witness. A macro names a machine as an artifact does, and a machine it names under which a check's gate decides otherwise withholds that check by the same rule.

defined.description: The architecture macros the dump defined, in the order listed: `__x86_64__` (machine `x86_64`), `__i386__` (`i386`), `__aarch64__` (`aarch64`), the families a check's architecture list names. Where `predefined_macros` is published and its dump completed, these are the ones it defines. Where that dump errored (`libc_headers_error` is present) or is empty, it is held only to define none outside these, since gcc prints no macros past a fatal `#include` while clang prints them all.

agreement.description: `agrees`: the dump defines the macro of `arch`'s machine family and no other. `disagrees`: it defines the macro of another family, or of more than one, or none where `arch` is of one of the three families, which witnesses a target outside them and withholds every arch-gated check; published with an error diagnostic under `toolchain.target`. `overruled`: it defines none of the three where `arch` is of one of their families, while every ELF artifact the run built carries `arch`'s family (`agreement: agrees`) and at least one of them was built by a probe of the dump's language (C++ for `profile_macros_cxx`, C otherwise), so the artifacts, the compiler's output, overrule the dump's silence; the evidence names a flag that suppresses the predefined macros (`-undef`, `-U` of the family's macro) as the cause where one is among the flags the dump was taken under, and otherwise, as for the flagless dump (`macros`), says the cause is not established; the dump witnesses no target and withholds nothing; a warning diagnostic under `toolchain.target`, apart from the one a contradicting witness carries. `unmapped`: `arch` names no machine family chard maps, and the dump defines one macro; a warning diagnostic where that macro's machine flips a gate. `no-arch-macro`: the dump defines none of the three and `arch` is of none of their families, which a target outside those families produces, and `arch` stands uncorroborated by this witness. `superseded`: `source` is `profile-macros`, so this dump, asked with no flags, names the driver's default target, which no probe was built for; `defined` is published and withholds nothing.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: The `ELF<class> <order>` the dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` (4 or 8) and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, where it defined both; published whatever the agreement, read by `abi` only where the agreement is `agrees`, and held to `predefined_macros` where `--emit-macros` published that dump. Absent where the dump failed, or defined one of the two or neither.

profile_macros.description: The third witness, present exactly where `profile.cflags` and `profile.ldflags` are not both empty: the same intrinsic dump taken under those flags, which witnesses a target they select on a run that reads no ELF artifact. A machine its macro names withholds by the rule `macros` does, for every C probe, and for every C++ probe where `profile_macros_cxx` is absent. The C flags alone: a target only `cxxflags` selects is `profile_macros_cxx`'s to witness, and the C++ probes' artifacts' where the run reads them.

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: `profile.cflags` then `profile.ldflags`, the list a C probe's measured variant is built with.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line (`build_record.stdout_unterminated`), whatever its exit status; its agreement is then `dump-failed`. Absent otherwise.

macros_defined.description: Every macro the dump defined, counted.

defined.description: The architecture macros this dump defined, in the order `macros.defined` lists them. Empty under `dump-failed`.

agreement.description: As `macros.agreement`, for the macros this dump defined, and `dump-failed`: the dump exited non-zero, defined no macro at all (a flag the driver refused), or exited 0 with its output cut off partway through a line (`stdout_unterminated`), so it witnesses nothing and `defined` is empty; never a target outside the three families.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, the flags, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: As `macros.abi`: the `ELF<class> <order>` this dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, where it defined both; absent where it defined one or neither.

profile_macros_cxx.description: The fourth witness, present exactly where `toolchain.cxx_driver` is present and the list a C++ probe's measured variant is built with (`profile.cxxflags`, or `profile.cflags` where that is empty, then `profile.ldflags`) differs from the C list `profile_macros` is taken under: the same intrinsic dump, through the C++ driver under that list, which witnesses a target only the C++ flags select on a run that reads no ELF artifact. A machine its macro names withholds by the rule `macros` does, and only the C++ probes' arch-gated checks, since the C probes were built under the C flags; a C++ probe is held to this dump in place of `profile_macros`. Absent where the lists are equal, since `profile_macros` then witnesses both, and where no C++ driver was found, since no C++ probe then builds. Taken whatever the probe selection, as `linker.cxx` is: it witnesses the profile's C++ flags, and on a selection with no C++ probe a `disagrees` withholds no verdict.

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: the list a C++ probe's measured variant is built with.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line (`build_record.stdout_unterminated`), whatever its exit status; its agreement is then `dump-failed`. Absent otherwise.

macros_defined.description: Every macro the dump defined, counted.

defined.description: The architecture macros this dump defined, in the order `macros.defined` lists them. Empty under `dump-failed`.

agreement.description: As `profile_macros.agreement`, for the macros this dump defined.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, the flags, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: As `macros.abi`: the `ELF<class> <order>` this dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, where it defined both; absent where it defined one or neither.

predefined_macros_sha256.description: Hash of the sorted `cc -dM -E` dump for the bare profile. Cheap fingerprint: two toolchains with equal hashes have identical macro-channel defaults.

predefined_macros.description: Optional full macro dump, name -> value (empty string when defined with no value).

fhardened_fortify.description: The driver's intrinsic macro dump under `-fhardened -O2` (`cc -fhardened -O2 -dM -E`, no profile flags), with its control under `-O2` alone (`baseline`), taken on every run, from which `fhardened-effective`'s fortify slot reads its bar where the dump answers what the option asks. It answers where the dump exited 0, its output was whole, it defined a macro and no line of its stderr names `-fhardened` or `-Whardened` (`diagnostic`), and the control exited 0, whole, defining a macro, and defines no `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, or one lower than the option's: clang refuses the token, gcc before 14 does not know it, gcc says so where a `-D` or `-U` of `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` from its own configuration overrode it, and a driver that defines the level whatever is asked (Alpine's gcc, Ubuntu's specs) leaves the option nothing to show. Where it answers, the bar is `fortify_source`, the level gcc picks from the glibc it was configured against, whatever the headers name; a dump that defines no `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, a value that is not an integer, or one outside 2 to 3, sets no bar. Where it does not, the bar is read from `environment.libc` and `target_triple`, and the slot's `note` says why the driver's reading was not used. A profile flag that changes the level `-fhardened` asks (`-specs=`, `-mmusl`, `--sysroot`) is outside this reading, since the dump takes none; the register entry `fhardened-dump-names-its-own-level` names what the reading trusts

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: `-fhardened`, `-O2`.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present and true where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line.

diagnostic.description: The first line of the dump's stderr naming `-fhardened` or `-Whardened`, verbatim.

fortify_source.description: The value the dump defined `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` to, verbatim.

baseline.description: The control: the same dump under `-O2` alone, without `-fhardened`. A level it defines equal to `fortify_source` is not the option's own, and a control that did not exit 0 whole, or defined no macro, attributes nothing.

libc_headers_error.description: Present when the dump of the libc-identification headers exited non-zero, whether or not it produced macros, or exited 0 with its output cut off partway through a line. Absent on a clean dump. On Darwin the unconditional `#include <features.h>` was a fatal error and clang dumped all 3047 macros regardless, so every macro-channel verdict there rested on the driver continuing past an error it called fatal, and nothing in the report said so. The include is guarded now; this field is what notices the next instance. Its text is `exited N`, or `was killed by a signal` where the compiler had no exit status, then `: ` and the first non-empty line of its stderr where it wrote one; for a dump that exited 0 with its output cut off, `exited 0 with its output cut off partway through a line`. Where it is present, `environment.libc.detection` names this failure: a library a macro of the dump names is still identified, since a dump that failed can lack macros and cannot gain them (a last line its output ended partway through, which the dump's end cut, is dropped, whatever the status), glibc's `version` only where `__GLIBC__` and `__GLIBC_MINOR__` both came out, and where no macro names a library `environment.libc.impl` is `unknown`.

profile.description: Which of the two-questions-never-to-conflate this report answers.

id.description: bare | bare-optimized | openssf-tldr | explicit:<digest>. "bare-optimized" is the compiler's own defaults plus -O2 and nothing else: fortify cannot instantiate without optimization, so a bare "--" is ambiguous between a compiler that sets nothing and one that sets it only when optimizing. A distribution's own build flags arrive through explicit: chard queries no package manager for them. The explicit id's suffix is twelve hex digits of a SHA-256 over cflags, cxxflags and ldflags, because this field is a column join key and two flag lists are two columns; the lists themselves are beside it in the clear. A run given --env pairs adds +env: and twelve hex digits of a SHA-256 over the pairs, sorted by name, each NAME=VALUE, NUL-separated: a toolchain configured through its environment is a different toolchain under each value, so two runs differing only in their pairs are two columns. The pairs are beside it in compiler_environment.set; a run with none has no suffix.

flags_sha256.description: A SHA-256 over `cflags`, `cxxflags` and `ldflags` in that order, each flag separated by U+001F and each list by a newline. Published on every profile, so two columns under one built-in id whose flags differ differ in a field a join can read; an explicit profile's id carries its first twelve digits.

flags_source.description: "none" is what makes a report a measurement of compiler-builtin defaults: no flag was passed and the driver loaded no configuration file. "driver-config-file" is the bare profile measured through a driver that loaded one (toolchain.config_files names it): no flag was passed, and the defaults measured are the compiler's compiled-in ones plus whatever that file supplies, which chard does not read. The third mechanism, between compiled-in defaults and a build system's flag injection; under "none" a hardening flag in such a file would be credited to the compiler. "chard-enabling-condition" means chard supplied a flag that grants no hardening itself but is a precondition for observing some — currently only -O2 — so a reader does not credit it to the distribution; a configuration file behind that profile is named in toolchain_note and in a diagnostic.

guide_revision.description: On the openssf-tldr profile only, and always there: the revision of the OpenSSF guide, by the date in its by-line (YYYY-MM-DD), whose rows the profile's flags are built from. The id stays openssf-tldr when the guide's rows change, and this field says which rows a report's profile was built from. It names the rows, not the flags: those also depend on the architecture the gate read (toolchain.target.arch) and on how chard composes the rows, so profile.cflags stays the record of what was passed. Absent on every other profile.

toolchain_note.description: How the query was made, and what was assumed if no selector was used.

compiler_environment.description: The complete environment every toolchain invocation of the run received: the toolchain's detection, its macro dumps and listings, and every probe build. chard clears its own environment and hands the compiler the variables named in passed and those in set, and nothing else; a probe's own run is described by its run record's environment instead. A toolchain configured through a variable (a Nix cc-wrapper's NIX_HARDENING_ENABLE) is measured as configured only where the variable is in set.

passed.description: Variables handed over from chard's own environment, by name: PATH where chard has one. The value is withheld because it names the operator's directories.

set.description: Variables set to a value, name to value: the pins every invocation receives (LC_ALL=C, TERM=dumb) and the run's --env pairs, which the operator wrote in the invocation. Every pair that is not a pin is in profile.id's +env: digest.

observations.description: One entry per probe. The raw facts; `matrix` is derived from these.

facts.description: The artifacts and `-dM -E` dumps the observations and their control arms were read from, stored once per digest and keyed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of what each entry describes: an artifact's bytes, `build.artifact_sha256`, or a dump's sorted lines, a dump record's `stdout_sha256`. Every observation's own build has an entry, whole, as does every built arm of a check on the `macro` or `elf-static` channel or of one that declares the ELF tables it reads, which may be an `elf-delta` against an observation's own build, every dump a macro-channel observation or arm read its macros from under `macro_source: preprocessor`, and every key a `decoded` reading names, the dump an `elf-static` predicate read its macros from among them; nothing else does, and `fact-store-disagrees-with-references` refuses a report whose references and entries disagree in either direction. `{}` when nothing was built. A reader meeting a `kind` outside the enumeration of `$defs/fact_entry` reads that entry as not understood, never as the absence of facts: a later revision may add kinds.

decoders.description: The predicates the readings in `observations` were evaluated with, once per report: every check that publishes a `decoded` reading has an entry, and no other check does. Absent when no reading was published.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the predicate's canonical form, compact `serde_json`, the digest `chard probes` publishes for the check's decoder.

fortify_ratchet.description: Derived view of the _FORTIFY_SOURCE rungs. The flag conflates two independent properties, and this block reports them separately because they are not always gated together: `whole_object_level` is how precisely an object can be bounded, and `dynamic_bounds` is whether sizes unknown at compile time are bounded at all. glibc gates the second behind the second rung of the first, so on glibc a single level describes both — which is why one number sufficed while glibc was the only implementation measured. fortify-headers (Alpine, Chimera) reaches dynamic sizing without subobject bounds at any level, which is not a point on glibc's ladder, and `implied_level` is therefore absent there. Under glibc, enforcement is cumulative and truthful readings are monotone: a non-monotone set cannot describe any real build and means a probe is faulty, so every derived field is withheld and the rungs' verdicts are downgraded rather than published.

implied_level.description: The coordinate on glibc's ladder, derived as a total function of the two axes: (0,no)->0, (1,no)->1, (2,no)->2, (2,yes)->3. ABSENT for any other combination — never null. A measurement off the ladder has no coordinate on it, which is a fact about the implementation rather than a gap in the measurement, and `implementation` names which one. Consumers gating on a level should read the axes instead where this is absent.

whole_object_level.description: How precisely the implementation can bound an object: `0` none, `1` whole-object only (__builtin_object_size(p,0)), `2` subobject — a struct member distinguished from the object enclosing it. Absent when no rung was decided.

dynamic_bounds.description: Whether sizes unknown at compile time are bounded, i.e. __builtin_dynamic_object_size rather than __builtin_object_size. Orthogonal to `whole_object_level`: fortify-headers reaches this without ever implementing subobject bounds, which is why treating it as a rung above level 2 made a report contradict itself. Absent when the rung was withheld.

implementation.description: The fortify implementation the rungs were measured against, from the probes' own .chard.report section. Only glibc nests the levels the way the ratchet assumes. `fortify-headers` (Alpine, Chimera) has no subobject bounds at any level, and level 3 swaps in __builtin_dynamic_object_size without adding the rung-2 distinction, so a dynamic rung firing while the subobject rung stays silent is that implementation working correctly rather than a broken probe. `apple` implements no level 3 at all: <secure/_common.h> clamps every request above 1 to 2, so the dynamic rung cannot fire. `freebsd` (15 and later, <ssp/ssp.h>) is Apple's shape: the request is clamped at 2 and only __builtin_object_size is asked. Absent when no probe reported one.

structured_diagnostics.description: Present only under `--structured-diagnostics`: the gate's count of its own work, against what was eligible, so a gate that compared nothing cannot read as agreement. Each disagreeing or undecodable arm is also a warning in `diagnostics`.

format.description: The side build's flag. Absent where no structured form is known for the toolchain, which a diagnostic also says.

checks_eligible.description: Observations of checks the structured decoder has needles for.

not_compared.description: Eligible checks with no comparison: withheld before their arms were built, or measured on a toolchain with no structured form. `checks_compared` plus this list's length is `checks_eligible`.

arms_expected.description: The arms the compared checks' comparisons were fed, summed: each comparison's `arms_expected`.

arms_missing.description: Of `arms_expected`, the arms with no build or no side build, which were not compared. `arms_compared` plus this is `arms_expected`, and the consistency rule `structured-diagnostics-disagrees-with-observations` recomputes every count here from the observations.

corroboration.description: Protections measured through more than one channel, and whether the channels agree. A macro claiming a protection is on while the artifact shows it absent is what a spec file patching one compiler job and not the other produces; that disagreement must be visible rather than resolved in favour of whichever channel was consulted.

verdicts.description: Only members that produced a measurement. A withheld verdict can neither corroborate nor contradict.

measured_channels.description: How many distinct channels actually produced a measurement. Not channels.length: a member withheld as probe-invalid, unsupported or build-failed contributes a channel to the group but no measurement, and cannot be one of the channels that agreed. Reporting channels.length instead announced "2 channel(s) agree" for a group where one channel had measured nothing. A `partial` at a level that instruments only code marked to opt in (`ssp-level` at `explicit`) is listed under `verdicts` and counts toward no channel here, since no probe opts in and nothing else can confirm or contradict it.

corroborated.description: True only when measured_channels >= 2, which is the sole condition under which the word corroborated means anything. Deliberately distinct from `agree`: one measuring channel plus one withheld member does not disagree, because a withheld verdict cannot contradict, but it is not corroborated either and the protection rests on a single channel. Measured on Debian 13, where the macro channel saw -fcf-protection requested and the artifact channel could not confirm any IBT or SHSTK property — requested but unverified, which is not the same as in force. A group whose only macro-channel member reads `partial` at an opt-in level (`ssp-level` at `explicit` under gcc's -fstack-protector-explicit) is not corroborated: that level rests on the macro channel alone.

withheld.description: Members that produced no measurement, mapped to the verdict that withheld them. Listed rather than dropped, so a reader can see which channel is blind and why.

sources.description: What each measuring member read, keyed by check. Withheld members are absent: they read nothing a verdict rests on, and `withheld` names them. A member reading `partial` at an opt-in level is absent too: `verdicts` lists it, and it is no witness the others are checked against.

witness.description: `artifact` for a member that read the probe's output: its headers, its `.chard.report` self-report, or a run of it. `preprocessor-dump` for a macro read from `cc -dM -E` because no artifact carried a self-report. `compiler-stderr` for a diagnostic stream.

artifact_sha256.description: The artifact the member read, or the build whose stderr it read. Absent for a preprocessor dump and wherever the build recorded no artifact.

independent_witnesses.description: How many distinct witnesses the measuring members read: one per build, keyed by its artifact digest, and one per preprocessor dump. A build's stderr and its artifact are one witness, two outputs of one compiler invocation. Not measured_channels: the macro, elf-static and runtime channels over one probe's build are three readers of one artifact, and a fault in that build reaches all three alike. Every witness is output of the same compiler and flag list, so this counts artifacts, not toolchains.

composites.description: Umbrella options answered by reducing over the measured checks rather than by probing for the option itself. Deliberately separate from `observations`: an observation is something a probe measured, a composite is arithmetic over those measurements, and a reader must be able to tell them apart. The reduction is three-valued — a constituent measured absent settles the umbrella regardless of any constituent that could not be measured, but an unmeasurable constituent prevents a positive verdict.

id.description: Stable identifier for the umbrella, e.g. `fhardened-effective`.

derived_from.description: Check ids this verdict was reduced from. Named so no reader mistakes the result for a measurement.

reason.description: Why this verdict, naming the constituents that decided it.

flag.description: The flag as the umbrella's own documentation names it.

check.description: The chard check consulted for this requirement. On `fhardened-effective`'s `-fstack-protector-strong` slot, `ssp-level-emitted`, the graded check, whose level the slot carries: the presence-only `canary-emitted` cannot tell plain `-fstack-protector` from `-strong`.

applicable.description: False where the requirement does not apply here at all, such as `-fcf-protection` off x86. Inapplicable constituents drop out of the reduction rather than counting as shortfalls.

level.description: Measured level, where the requirement is about strength rather than presence. On `fhardened-effective`'s `-fstack-protector-strong` slot, `ssp-level-emitted`'s level wherever that check published one: `explicit`, `basic`, `strong`, `all`, or `unsafe-frame`.

satisfied.description: DEPRECATED, retained for one schema generation: true only when state is `in-force` or `marked`. Read `state` instead — a false here does not distinguish measured-absent from could-not-establish.

note.description: Why, when the requirement is unsatisfied or inapplicable. Distinguishes a constituent measured absent from one that could not be established. On `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot it is present in every state and names the reading that set the bar (the driver's `-fhardened -O2` dump, or the C library and why the dump did not answer), or why none was set; `bar` beside it carries the level and the reading as values.

implementation.description: The C library's fortify implementation the slot was read under, where the reading depends on it: on `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot where `fortify-effective`'s measured reading was decided by one of its two fortify-headers level clauses, `fortify-headers` (a request of 2 or below) or `fortify-headers-dynamic-request` (above 2) (Alpine, Chimera). fortify-headers implements level 1 alone, whatever is requested, since its checks never ask a subobject's bounds, so the slot reads `in-force` where the level `fortify-requested` read (`requested_level`) meets the bar, with a note saying so, and the constituent's `level` stays the library's 1.

name.description: The implementation `fortify-effective`'s deciding clause identifies. It is always `fortify-headers`, whichever of the two level clauses decided; the clause itself is the observation's `evidence.decoded.clause`. An open vocabulary: an implementation added later adds a name without a schema change.

top_level.description: The highest level the implementation enforces: `1`.

requested_level.description: The level `fortify-requested` read, verbatim, where that check is `on` or `partial`; absent otherwise, and then the request meets no bar.

bar.description: The bar `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot was held to, as a value beside the `note` that names it in words: a `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` level, and which reading set it. Present where a reading set a bar and absent where none did, and the `note` says why. The consistency rule `fhardened-fortify-slot-disagrees-with-inputs` recomputes it with the slot's `state`, `level` and `implementation` from `toolchain.fhardened_fortify`, `environment.libc`, `toolchain.target_triple` and the two fortify observations, at publication and on read, and holds a driver's bar to the level its dump defined apart from that recomputation.

level.description: The level: where `source` is `driver`, the one the dump defined; where it is `library`, 3 from glibc 2.35 and 2 below it and on musl.

source.description: `driver`: the level this driver's own `-fhardened -O2` dump defined (`toolchain.fhardened_fortify.fortify_source`), held to its `-O2` control: what `-fhardened` asks of a build here. `library`: the level gcc's `-fhardened` would ask on the C library `environment.libc` and `toolchain.target_triple` name, read where the dump did not answer (a driver that refuses the option, as clang does, among them): a statement about the option on this library, not a reading of this compiler.

opt_out.description: A program header in the artifact the constituent's check measured by which the program opts out of what the marking asks for. `cfi-effective` alone reads one, OpenBSD's PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI (`facts[...].elf.openbsd_nobtcfi`): with it the constituent is `absent` where `environment.libc.impl` is `openbsd`, whose kernel was measured honouring it, and `not-established` for a marked artifact elsewhere, while `verdict` keeps the marking's own reading. `composite-verdict-disagrees-with-constituents` holds it to the store in both directions, and holds a constituent naming it to `absent` under OpenBSD's C library and to anything but `in-force` or `marked` under another.

facts.description: The `facts` key of the artifact carrying the header: the cited observation's `build.artifact_sha256`.

state.description: Three-valued plus inapplicable, matching the reduction this block documents. `absent` is measured absence; `not-established` means the constituent could not be measured and the umbrella therefore cannot be confirmed. Replaces a required boolean `satisfied`, which collapsed those two into one value in the block most likely to be read as a summary. `marked`: the constituent's check reads a marking the artifact carries, `cet-marked` or `branch-protection-marked`, by which the program asks the kernel, CPU and C library for a protection whose enforcement the constituent does not measure; it is confirmed in the reduction as `in-force` is, so `cfi-effective` and `fhardened-effective` read `on` over it, and the `note` says what the report measured of enforcement (`shadow-stack-enforced`'s reading on x86; on aarch64 that no check measures BTI or PAC enforcement; under OpenBSD's C library what its kernel does: on arm64 BTI is enforced for every program without `PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI`, marked or not, and on amd64 the header turns IBT enforcement off). `cfi-effective`'s constituent and `fhardened-effective`'s `-fcf-protection=full` slot read `marked` and never `in-force`, which `composite-verdict-disagrees-with-constituents` holds at publication.

defect_coverage.description: Derived view keyed by what a flag protects against rather than by flag. This is the view an incident asks for: a flag list does not answer whether a given primitive is closed.

status.description: Read from the bearing checks that observe protection (`observations[].observes`); a request or marking is tallied under its own key and moves the status in no direction. mitigated: every bearing check produced a verdict, every one observing protection read a full on, and at least one did. partial: some protection but not all of it, including a partial verdict, a mix of on and off, or an on beside a withheld check. not-mitigated: a bearing check observed protection absent and none observed it present. unknown: no bearing check observed protection or its absence: each withheld, a request or a marking. NOTE the asymmetry, and read `complete` alongside: `mitigated` requires every bearing check to have been decided, `not-mitigated` does not, so a single `off` beside four withheld checks yields `not-mitigated` from a fifth of the evidence.

complete.description: Whether every bearing check produced a verdict, a request's or marking's own key counted as one. `status` alone does not carry it, and the two directions are not symmetric — see the note on `status`. A consumer treating `not-mitigated` as a finding about the defect class should require this. `true` beside `unknown` is a class borne by requests or markings alone (`jump-oriented-programming`, whose summary says so): a gap in the corpus, not in the measurement, and not a finding.

verdict_counts.description: One key per bearing check: its verdict in protection terms (a weaken check's off counts as on) where it observes protection, and `requested` or `marked` (its verdict on or partial), `not-requested` or `not-marked` (off) where it observes a request or a marking; a withheld verdict keeps its name either way.

coverage.description: Mandatory. Count what was fed and compare to the corpus total: a check that was never handed to the harness cannot report its own absence. `checks_expected` is what this run selected; `corpus_checks_total` is what exists.

checks_expected.description: Distinct check ids the selection named, counted as a set: a repeated `--probe` is refused at the door, and the reconciliation against `observations` is by id (see `checks_missing` and `checks_unexpected`) as well as by count, because a list of the right length can still have measured one check twice and another not at all.

checks_attempted.description: The length of `observations`. Held equal to the `verdict_counts` total, and to the number of distinct check ids, by the `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` rule.

checks_valid.description: Probes whose controls discriminated, so whose verdict is trustworthy.

checks_skipped.description: Expected ids with no observation, counted; `checks_missing` names them.

checks_missing.description: Check ids the selection named and no observation carries. Absent when empty, which is every healthy run.

checks_unexpected.description: Check ids an observation carries and the selection never named. Absent when empty; present, it is a harness fault the consistency pass refuses.

checks_not_applicable_here.description: Checks the target architecture puts out of reach: those the architecture gate withheld under `arch-gated`. `target-arch-contradicted` and `target-abi-contradicted` also name the architecture in `gating.arch`; a check they withhold is an unread premise, counted among `withholding.instrument_withholdings`, not here. The gate decides from the mechanism table (`src/mechanism.rs`), keyed on the question a check answers, and publishes `arch-gated` only where the target answers that question with another mechanism a check reads: the CET marking checks (cet-macro, cet-marked, cet-marked-object, cet-endbr-emitted) off x86_64 and x86, where aarch64 answers with BTI, PAC and GCS, and the branch-protection and GCS pairs off aarch64, where x86_64 and x86 answer with CET. A check whose mechanism the target has and no check reads there (`no-check-on-target`), or whose target the table has no row for (`arch-outside-table`), is withheld as `indeterminate`, sets no `gating.arch`, and is not counted here: on aarch64 shadow-stack-enforced, textrel-absent and linker-default-noexecstack, and on x86 shadow-stack-enforced, noexecstack-enforced, ubsan-trap-mode, fortify-printf-flag and zero-call-used-regs, whose constructions are written for other architectures. `chard probes` lists each check's gate. Each is an earned limitation, counted in `withholding.earned_limitations` under `arch-gated`, and settles `all_verdicts_published`, because no single host can attempt both groups and a gate that can never pass is one nobody runs. This count was once the denominator of `all_checks_valid` (corpus_checks_total minus this), where architecture was exempt and libc was not; that field is removed, and a libc limitation such as Alpine's `unsupported` fortify is an earned limitation as this is.

verdict_counts.description: verdict -> count over all observations. Sums to checks_attempted, held by the `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` rule.

profile_flags_unexamined.description: Profile flags no check in this report examines, in the profile's own spelling and order. The corpus is one denominator and the profile's flag list is the other: an `openssf-tldr` report with fifteen `on` cells and half the guide's flags matched by no check read as the guide honoured. A profile flag and a check's `flag` are matched through a key (`-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3` and `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` reach `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE`; `-fcf-protection` reaches `-fcf-protection=full`; `-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now` reaches the RELRO check; a `-W` flag matches exactly; `--param` and its argument are one flag, keyed on the parameter's name; an optimization level keys on `-O` as written, so `-o` is the output option), against the observations this report carries, so a `--probe`-filtered run names what it left unexamined. Absent when empty, and an empty list means every profile flag reached at least one observation, whatever that observation's verdict: a flag whose only cell is `build-failed` or `probe-invalid` counts as examined, so this is a weaker claim than every flag having a verdict, and `verdict_counts` is where the verdicts are. Named in `truncations` when not empty; held to the profile and the observations by the `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` rule.

truncations.description: Anything deliberately capped, sampled, or dropped. Silent truncation reads as full coverage; it must be recorded here.

corpus_checks_total.description: Total checks in the embedded corpus, independent of any --probe filter. `complete` is judged against THIS, not against the selected count, so a filtered run cannot report itself complete.

all_checks_attempted.description: checks_attempted == corpus_checks_total. Renamed from `complete`, which was a conclusion in a field holding only a count comparison, and was read `true` alongside `probe-invalid: 6` — attempting a check is not answering it.

all_verdicts_published.description: Every check in the corpus was attempted and settled: published a measurement (on, off, partial) or an earned limitation (`withholding.earned_limitations`). chard answered every question it could pose, so this is `all_checks_attempted` with `withholding.instrument_withholdings` empty, which the `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` rule holds when the report is written and when it is read, and a run whose only non-measurements are earned limitations reads true. What --fail-on-missing gates on, and it answers whether the run was complete rather than whether the build is hardened. A check withheld under `no-check-on-target` or `arch-outside-table` is a measurement chard does not have, not a limitation of the target: it is an instrument withholding, so on a target where the mechanism table has a row no check reads (aarch64, x86) or no row at all, this is false whatever else the run measured, and `--fail-on-missing` fails, until a check reads those mechanisms there. `all_checks_valid`, which once stood beside this, is removed: it asked whether every triple outside the architecture gates discriminated, which an earned `unsupported` over a flag the driver does not know never does, so it read false on an ordinary run; `checks_valid` keeps the count, and a triple that failed outside an earned limitation is counted in `instrument_withholdings`.

evidence_filters.description: What the per-observation evidence was trimmed to, by field. Mandatory: a filter a report does not name is a reader told the evidence is complete.

macros.description: The name list `observations[].evidence.macros` is trimmed to. The full dump is thousands of names and `--emit-macros` keeps it once, under `toolchain.predefined_macros`; every macro-channel observation carries only the names here, and cites this list's digest as `evidence.macros_filter`. A macro absent from `evidence.macros` is therefore either undefined or outside this list, and this block is what tells the two apart.

symbols.description: The names the ELF reader looks for in a symbol table (`elf::WATCHED_SYMBOLS`). Every stored `elf.watched_symbols` holds only these, so a name outside the list is one the reader never looked for rather than one the artifact lacks; the Published view answers a symbol read against this list and no other.

consistency.description: Whether this report's derived fields agree with the observations under them, and which of them were checked. The derived fields — fortify_ratchet, defect_coverage, composites — are arithmetic computed over observations, and every other self-check works within a layer: a control triple validates one check, corroboration compares channels within one protection, reconcile compares two documents. `rules_applied` is published because no contradictions under one rule and no contradictions under all of them are very different claims, and the findings alone cannot distinguish them, as a `coverage.complete` that compared the selection against itself could not. A contradiction is a fault in chard rather than a finding about the toolchain.

status.description: What the rules in `rules_applied` concluded: `contradicted` when `contradictions` holds any entry, `consistent` when it holds none. Derived from that list where the report is serialized, so the two agree in every report chard writes. A report carrying `contradicted` is never written to the requested path or to stdout: given `-o`, it is written to `<output>.contradicted`, and without one, nowhere. `consistent` is as strong as `rules_applied` and `fields_checked` say it is.

rules_applied.description: Rule ids that ran, in the order applied. `derived-fortify-level-exceeds-measured`: the ratchet derived a level above the one the C library reported settling on, or a level on either side that is not a whole number; or the ratchet is not the one its rung observations give: absent beside a rung, `rungs` not those observations in ladder order with their verdicts, `monotone` not the absence of an `inconsistency`, a non-monotone ratchet beside a measured rung, an axis other than the one the rung verdicts establish, or an `implied_level` other than the point of glibc's ladder its own axes land on. `dynamic-bounds-without-whole-object-bounds`: dynamic object sizes reported in force while no whole-object bounding is, which cannot hold because the dynamic rung answers how big an object is. `defect-status-disagrees-with-bearing-checks`: a defect's status is not the one its own bearing verdicts license (a request or marking, keyed under `requested`, `marked`, `not-requested` or `not-marked`, licenses nothing either way), or the rollup's counts are not a recount of the observations declaring the defect (a request or marking counted as protection among them), or an observation's `observes` is not the bearing table's word for its check, or is absent, in a report of this corpus, or is written on some observations and not others, or the rollup names a check the report does not carry, or a check declares a defect the rollup has no entry for or whose entry does not name it. `composite-verdict-disagrees-with-constituents`: an umbrella claims a
