fields_checked.description: Derived fields this pass examined. A derived field absent from this list was not checked, whatever `contradictions` says.

contradictions.description: Claims in this report that contradict other claims in it. Always present, `[]` when the rules listed above found none.

rule.description: Stable id of the rule that fired, so a consumer can gate on a class rather than on prose. `derived-fortify-level-exceeds-measured`: the ratchet derived a level above the one the C library reported settling on, which claims a rung the same document says was never reached.

property.description: The property both claims are about.

replay.description: What `decoded-reading-disagrees-with-facts` fed itself against what it replayed: `readings` is `replayed + unresolved` plus the length of `not_replayable`.

replayed.description: Re-evaluated with the Published view and compared.

unresolved.description: Not evaluated because a `facts` key or entry, or the check's `decoders` entry, is missing or of the wrong kind, or evaluated to a key the facts do not hold; each is named by a contradiction.

not_replayable.description: Readings the Published view stopped at a macro a `c-int` term reached by following a mode value to a name `evidence_filters.macros` does not keep, as with `-D_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE=MYMODE -DMYMODE=4` in a preprocessor-sourced map. Not a contradiction: the trimmed map says nothing about that name.

diagnostics.description: Harness-level problems that are not attributable to a single probe. A diagnostic with the context `profile-flag-rejected` names one profile flag the toolchain rejected and carries `rejection`; those come first, the one with the most `cells_withheld` first, then by tool and flag. There is one per program the refusal line names and flag it refused: a flag gcc and g++ both refuse is two, one linker refusing a `-Wl,` flag for every probe is one, and a build that refused two flags counts in both.

rejection.description: Present only on a `profile-flag-rejected` warning: one tool and one profile flag it refused, counted over the `build-failed` observations whose published build it refused that flag in (on any refusal line; `build_rejection` names the first). A macro-channel observation whose preprocessor dump the flag refused reads `indeterminate` and is not counted. It says whose flag it was and what the tool said, not whether the flag is misspelt or newer than the toolchain, which one toolchain cannot tell apart. The `profile-flag-rejection-disagrees-with-observations` consistency rule recomputes it.

tool.description: The program the refusal line names (`gcc`, `g++`, `clang`, `cc1`, a linker's path), or `the toolchain` where the line opens with none.

flag.description: The profile flag refused, as the tool spelled it: a linker names `--no-such-option` for a profile's `-Wl,--no-such-option`.

supplied_by.description: `built-in-profile`: a profile chard builds, named by `profile.id`, supplies the flag, so this toolchain rejects a flag of that profile. `operator`: `--profile explicit`, so the operator's `--flags`, `--cxxflags` or `--ldflags` supplied it.

line.description: The line the build of the observation `first_check` names refused the flag on, as published in `build.stderr`, relative to the work directory.

first_check.description: The first observation, in report order, whose published build this tool refused this flag in.

cells_withheld.description: The `build-failed` observations whose published build this tool refused this flag in.

cells_attempted.description: Every observation in the report, `coverage.checks_attempted`: the frame for `cells_withheld`.

linker.description: The linker the profile links with. Detected from the driver's `-###` link line under the profile's own `-fuse-ld=`, `--ld-path=` and `-B` flags, so a selection a wrapper or a configuration file adds is read too; where the line names no link, from `-print-prog-name`, which ignores the first two in both drivers, under the same flags. `artifact` is required because every published report runs the cross-check; a report without it would be one where the artifacts were never asked.

version.description: First line of the linker's own --version output. Absent where it printed none, or where that job did not exit 0 with its output whole (`kind` is then `unknown` and `detection` says how it ended).

path.description: Absolute wherever it could be resolved; absent where it was not, as where the driver's `-print-prog-name` did not exit 0 with its answer whole (`detection` says why). A bare `ld` is a name a reader cannot follow, so when the driver prints one chard resolves it on PATH, as the driver's own link step would, and `path_source` says so.

path_source.description: Who turned the name into `path`: the driver printed it, as the program its `-###` link line runs or in answer to `-print-prog-name` (`driver`), the driver printed a bare name and chard searched PATH (`path-search`), or the profile named the file through `--ld-path=` or `-fuse-ld=/path` (`profile`). Present exactly when `path` is.

profile_flags.description: The profile flags consulted, as written: `-B` prefixes, `-fuse-ld=` and `--ld-path=`. Absent when the profile selected nothing and the driver's default is the linker reported.

detection.description: How the linker identity was determined, in prose: the query the driver was asked, what it printed, and who resolved it, recorded so a reader can judge how much to trust it.

artifact.description: The linked artifacts' testimony against `kind`. Every producer that touched an object appends a line to its `.comment` section: the compiler by default (`-fno-ident` withholds it), lld as `Linker: <vendor> LLD <version>` and mold as `mold <version> (compatible with GNU ld)`, both surviving `-s` and `-Wl,--strip-all` (measured 2026-09-28: lld 14.0.0, 15.0.7, 18.1.3 and 22.1.8 and mold 1.0.3, 2.30.0 and 2.40.4, in the docker.io/library/ubuntu:22.04 and ubuntu:24.04 images and on Fedora 44 aarch64). GNU ld 2.42 and 2.46.1 and gold 1.16 write nothing of their own, so a `bfd` or `gold` banner can only ever be uncontradicted by this mechanism. `kind` stays the banner's word whatever the artifacts said; a consumer that needs the artifacts' answer gates on `agreement`.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every linked artifact carries one linker line naming the banner's kind and version. `disagrees`: the artifacts name another linker or version than the banner, two artifacts name different linkers, or the banner names lld or mold and no artifact carries the line those two always write; published beside the banner with an error diagnostic under `toolchain.linker`, and `consistency.contradictions` stays empty. `artifact-only`: every linked artifact carries one linker line and no --version banner chard read names a linker it recognises (`kind` is `unknown`: the program printed no banner, one outside the grammar, or failed `--version`, or no linker path was read), so the artifact is the only witness and its line is `signature`; a warning diagnostic, since the gap is in what chard read of the linker. `no-signature`: no artifact carries a linker line and the banner names a linker that writes none (GNU ld, gold) or none chard recognises, so the banner stands uncorroborated. `no-linked-artifact`: nothing was counted, either because no linked ELF artifact was read in this run (a Mach-O host, a probe selection that builds nothing, or a run whose every link failed) or because every artifact read was left uncounted and is named in `evidence` under its reason; `artifacts_read` is 0 and the evidence opens with which of the two it was.

signature.description: The `.comment` line that named a linker, when one did.

artifacts_read.description: Distinct linked artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, whose `.comment` was read to its end. Relocatables (no linker produced them), artifacts whose `.comment` could not be read or looked up, and the clean-build artifact of a check that measures the toolchain default under a profile whose link line selects a linker (linked under the driver's default, without the selection the evidence quotes) are named in `evidence` and not counted, and so are the probes that contributed no artifact. Under a profile whose flags select no linker, `bare-optimized` among the built-in ones, both builds go through the same link line and the clean-build artifact counts.

evidence.description: Which artifacts, what their `.comment` carried, and why the verdict follows: on `disagrees`, the first disagreeing pair and the count of the rest; then the artifacts left uncounted, each under its reason, and the probes that contributed no readable artifact.

cxx.description: The linker the C++ probes were linked with, present only when the profile's cxxflags select a different one from the C link (`-fuse-ld=`, `--ld-path=` or `-B` in cxxflags alone, or a different selection there). Queried through the C++ driver, whose `-B` and `-print-prog-name` search the C++ link goes through. Absent when no C++ driver sits beside the C one, since no C++ link ran; the C linker's `detection` records the selection then. Its `artifact` is held to the C++ probes' artifacts alone, and it never carries a `cxx` of its own.

verdict.description: `off` is a positive claim requiring proof that the observable would have appeared; it is never the default for a failed measurement.

argv.description: Full compiler invocation, re-runnable from inside the work directory: every path under that directory is recorded relative to it, so `-o probe probe.c` here was `-o <workdir>/probe <workdir>/probe.c` at the driver. The driver was invoked with the absolute spelling, because the operator's own flags resolve against the operator's directory.

dropped_flags.description: Profile flags removed before this build because they cannot coexist with the probe's output kind — `-pie` against `-shared`, and its siblings. Absent when nothing was removed, which is almost every build. Present, it is what reconciles `profile.cflags` with `argv`: without it a build that used a different flag list than the profile names says so nowhere, and a reader cannot tell a deliberate conflict resolution from a harness bug.

stderr.description: Truncated compiler diagnostics; the observable itself for the compiler-diag channel. Paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary object names (/tmp/ccXXXXXX.o and its clang and Apple spellings) read `<compiler-temp>`; both rewrites apply to this published copy only, and the detectors read the stream as captured.

stdout.description: The job's standard output. For a `-dM -E` dump record (`evidence.macro_dump` and the arms' `macro_dump`) the defines are replaced by a one-line note giving their count: `evidence.macros` carries the filtered map and `--emit-macros` keeps the toolchain-level dump once, and eight cells each carrying 200 KB of defines was a 1.7 MB report for one probe.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock lifetime of the child process. Whole milliseconds, so `0` means the process finished in under a millisecond rather than that it was not timed.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where text other than whitespace followed the job's last newline on standard output (or made up the whole output where it printed none); absent otherwise. Read before `stdout` is stored with its trailing whitespace trimmed. A `-dM -E` listing ends each define with a newline (every dump measured, gcc 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16 and clang 14, 18, 22 and 23 on Linux and Apple clang 21 on macOS), so a dump record carrying it was cut off partway through its last line, for example by a closed pipe, a signal or a full disk, and its status may say nothing of it: gcc 16.1.1's driver exits 0 when its `cc1` dies of a closed pipe under `-wrapper` (Fedora 44 x86_64). The last line is not read as a define, and the dump is read as failed: a variant's macro checks are withheld, the intrinsic dump is refused, the with-headers dump is named in `toolchain.libc_headers_error`, and a dump under the profile's flags is `dump-failed`.

stdout_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the job's standard output with its lines sorted bytewise and joined by newlines, with no newline after the last, on a `-dM -E` dump record, where `stdout` is replaced by a count of the defines: the key of the dump's `macro-dump` entry in `facts`. The same value is `LC_ALL=C sort` over the dump with its final newline removed, then SHA-256. Over the sorted lines so that it moves only where a line does: gcc lists its macros in identifier-table order, which an added `-D` can reshuffle with no macro changed.

exit_status.description: -1 when the process did not exit normally; see `signal`.

signal.description: Terminating signal name, e.g. SIGABRT, SIGSEGV, SIGILL, SIGTRAP. Two detectors key on a bare trap: __builtin_trap() is ud2 on x86_64, raising SIGILL, and brk on aarch64, raising SIGTRAP, so the same mechanism reaches the report under either name depending on the architecture. Numbering is per-platform; the name is resolved on the host that ran the probe.

stdout.description: The probe's standard output. On Darwin a probe whose reading rests on the machine opens it with one `CHARD-TRANSLATION` line, its read of `sysctl.proc_translated` (`0`, `1`, or `unreadable` with the failure), which `run-under-emulation` reads on a macOS run. One value in it varies between runs of one artifact, listed under x-volatile-readings by the check whose run prints it and the text before it; under --normalize its digits read `<volatile>` here, in that check's `evidence.observed` and in its control arms' `detail`.

stderr.description: Where glibc's "*** buffer overflow detected ***" and friends land.

timed_out.description: Whether `deadline_ms` elapsed before chard saw the probe exit. A probe that exited in the window between the deadline and the kill keeps its real status beside this flag and is read; one the kill ended (`signal` `SIGKILL`, or no status) never finished writing, and a runtime reading over it is withheld under `run-deadline-elapsed`.

deadline_ms.description: The deadline this run was held to, in whole milliseconds: `--timeout`, applied to each probe run, and the same value as `run.deadlines.probe_run_ms`. `timed_out` is read against it.

output_error.description: Why an output stream could not be read. Absent on every healthy run. Present means `stdout` or `stderr` is empty because chard failed to read the file, NOT because the probe was silent — and on the runtime and compiler-diag channels those are opposite measurements. A detector must not read a verdict from an empty stream when this is present. A runtime check over such a run is withheld under `run-output-unreadable`.

output_truncated.description: A stream hit the 16 KiB capture cap and lost its tail, so a diagnostic appearing late in the output is absent from this record for a reason that is chard's rather than the probe's. A runtime check over such a run is withheld under `run-output-unreadable`, and a control arm over one reads `indeterminate` with the cut named in its `detail`.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock lifetime of the child process. Whole milliseconds, so `0` means the process finished in under a millisecond rather than that it was not timed.

environment.description: The complete environment the probe received, name to value. chard clears the ambient environment before running a probe and sets exactly these: the pins every probe receives, and any the probe itself declares (`run_environment` in `chard probes`; `shadow-stack` declares `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.cpu.hwcaps=SHSTK:glibc.malloc.perturb=170`), so no loader, allocator or sanitizer variable from the host reached it. A reader re-deriving a runtime verdict runs the artifact under this map and nothing more.

symbol_fact.description: One symbol-table entry, reduced to what a detector asks about. The key it sits under in `watched_symbols` is the name before the first `@`.

defined.description: false is SHN_UNDEF, a reference satisfied at load time. A canary-protected binary references __stack_chk_fail; one that statically links libssp defines it, and a detector tells those apart.

tables.description: The symbol tables that carried the name, by section name (`.symtab`, `.dynsym`), or `SHT_SYMTAB` / `SHT_DYNSYM` for a table whose name could not be read. A stripped binary has only `.dynsym`, so an absent symbol there is weaker evidence.

versioned.description: The versioned spellings the tables stored (`__stack_chk_fail@GLIBC_2.4`, or `name@@VERSION` for a default version), so what the key cut is kept. Present only when at least one table stored a version; absent when every table stored the name bare.

fact_entry.description: One entry of `facts`, tagged by `kind`. `elf`: an artifact the reader accepted, carrying `elf`, the reader's whole account of it (`$defs/elf_facts`, `.chard.report` included as `self_report`), byte-comparable with `chard elf` on the same file but for `truncations`, which the entry carries always, `[]` included, and `chard elf` omits when empty. `unreadable`: an artifact that linked and that the reader refused, carrying `error`, the reader's reason with the artifact's path replaced by `<artifact>`, since the key names the bytes and two builds with equal bytes are one entry, and `mach_o`, `true` where the reader refused the bytes as a Mach-O object and absent otherwise: the macro channel reads the `-dM -E` dump by design over such an artifact on a macOS run, and over no other artifact the reader refused. `elf-delta`: an arm's artifact the reader accepted, carrying `base`, the key of an observation's own build stored as `elf`, and `elf_changes`, the members of `$defs/elf_facts` whose values differ from the base's; the arm's facts are the base's with each of those members in place of its own, and never an observation's own build's; an empty list or map in place of a member the base carries and `$defs/elf_facts` omits when empty resolves to that member's absence. `macro-dump`: a `-dM -E` dump, carrying `defines`, `macros_filter` and `macros`. Each kind carries exactly its own members; the validator that holds the schema to the code implements no conditional keyword, so `tests/schema_conformance.rs` holds each recorded entry's members to its kind.

base.description: The key of the `elf` entry an `elf-delta` is stated against: an observation's own `build.artifact_sha256`.

elf_changes.description: The members of `$defs/elf_facts`, as serialized, whose values in the arm's facts differ from `base`'s. A member `$defs/elf_facts` omits when empty, which the base carries and the arm does not, is stated as the empty list or map, and resolves to the member's absence, never to the empty value, which `$defs/elf_facts` refuses for a member declared with `minItems: 1`; `openbsd_nobtcfi`, omitted when false, is stated as `false` and resolves to its absence the same way. `tests/schema_conformance.rs` holds each recorded delta, laid over its base, to `$defs/elf_facts`.

defines.description: How many `#define` lines the dump printed: the count its published record's `stdout` names.

macros_filter.description: `evidence_filters.macros.sha256`: the filter `macros` was trimmed through, the same one an observation's inline `evidence.macros` passes through.

macros.description: The dump's defines that survive the filter, name to value (empty string when defined with no value).

elf_facts.description: Everything the elf-static channel reads from one artifact, as `elf::ElfFacts` serializes it: the header facts, the nine link facts, the dynamic-section flags and lists, the property markings, the symbol facts and the two recorded strings. Every member is required except `gnu_property_notes` and `truncations`, which are absent when empty where `elf::ElfFacts` is serialized on its own, and a symbol's `versioned` list; a `facts` entry of kind `elf` carries `truncations` always, `[]` included, which `tests/schema_conformance.rs` holds per entry. The nine link facts whose type admits `null` (`pie`, `static_pie`, `shared_object`, `statically_linked`, `relro`, `gnu_relro`, `bind_now`, `gnu_stack_present`, `gnu_stack_executable`) are `null` together on an object the loader cannot run and carry a value together on every ET_EXEC and ET_DYN; `df_1_pie` between them is the linker's own flag and stays a boolean. The reader holds that rule; the validator that holds the schema to the code implements no conditional keyword, so `tests/schema_conformance.rs` counts the nine per recorded instance and holds each instance to zero or nine `null` members.

elf_class.description: EI_CLASS, the width of the file's addresses and offsets. `machine` names the family without it, so `ppc64` covers a ppc64le object; with `elf_data` it is what `toolchain.target.abi` holds the artifact to.

elf_data.description: EI_DATA, the byte order every field of the file was read in, which is the order its target reads memory in. Written by every live read. A record without it is left out of `toolchain.target.abi.artifacts` by the target witness, which names it, and the execution witness withholds on it. With `elf_class` it tells `ppc64` from ppc64le and `aarch64` from aarch64_be, and `env::runs_natively` holds it to the kernel's own order.

elf_type.description: e_type by name: ET_NONE, ET_REL, ET_EXEC, ET_DYN or ET_CORE. Any other value reads `unrecognised (e_type 0x..)`, with `OS-specific` or `processor-specific` named when the value falls in that range, so a classifier that compares against a name never matches a number it has not seen.

machine.description: e_machine as the family's short name: i386, mips, ppc, ppc64, s390, arm, x86_64, aarch64, riscv or loongarch. Any other value reads `unrecognised (e_machine 0x..)`. Width and byte order are `elf_class` and `elf_data`.

has_interp.description: A PT_INTERP segment names a loader.

has_dynamic.description: The dynamic section was found and carries at least one entry.

pie.description: ET_DYN plus one of the linker-recorded DF_1_PIE, a PT_INTERP, or a DT_DEBUG entry (`dt_debug`); ET_DYN alone cannot separate a PIE from a shared library. This and the eight nullable link facts after it, `static_pie` through `gnu_stack_executable` (`df_1_pie` between them stays a boolean), are `null` together on an object the loader cannot run (an e_type other than ET_EXEC or ET_DYN): a relocatable object has no loader to be position-independent for and no segment for RELRO to cover, so `null` is a measured statement that the observable is out of the artifact's reach. The key is always present, which separates this from the absent-key rule on an observation's `level`. A detector that reads one of these returns no reading on `null`, and the observation is withheld: `indeterminate`, or `not-applicable` under `artifact-cannot-carry-observable` where the check's precondition on the artifact fails (a dynamic section for `relro`; position-independent output for `relative-relocs`, a shared object for `nodlopen`, and a `DT_NEEDED` entry naming the C library beside a dynamic section for `as-needed`, whatever the classification; `relative-relocs` and `nodlopen` are read from these link facts, `relro` from `has_dynamic`, and `as-needed` from `has_dynamic` and `needed`).

df_1_pie.description: DF_1_PIE in DT_FLAGS_1, the linker's own record of a PIE link; false on an object with no dynamic flags.

static_pie.description: ET_DYN with no interpreter and DF_1_PIE or DT_DEBUG, either of which marks executable output; DT_SONAME does not override the mark. Without a marker an interpreter-less ET_DYN is an ordinary shared library, so requiring one keeps every `.so` out of this column. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

shared_object.description: ET_DYN with a dynamic section, no interpreter, and neither DF_1_PIE nor DT_DEBUG. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

statically_linked.description: No loader runs it: an ET_EXEC with no interpreter, a static PIE, which carries a dynamic section to relocate itself, or an ET_DYN with neither an interpreter nor a dynamic section, which nothing could load. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

relro.description: `full` is a PT_GNU_RELRO segment with `bind_now`, `partial` the segment without it, `none` no segment. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`. Pinned against `elf::RELRO_LEVELS`.

gnu_relro.description: A PT_GNU_RELRO segment is present. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

bind_now.description: Immediate binding under any of its three spellings: a DT_BIND_NOW entry, DF_BIND_NOW in DT_FLAGS, or DF_1_NOW in DT_FLAGS_1. bfd emits DT_FLAGS only when it is non-zero, so a conformant link may record the request under one spelling alone. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

gnu_stack_present.description: A PT_GNU_STACK segment is present. A missing segment defers to the kernel's default and is a different fact from a non-executable stack, so a detector reads it as unmeasured. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

gnu_stack_executable.description: PF_X on the PT_GNU_STACK segment; false when `gnu_stack_present` is false. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`. The last PT_GNU_STACK where there are several, the one Linux acts on; where they disagree on PF_X, `truncations` carries an `unread` `gnu-stack` entry, which only `noexecstack` and `linker-default-noexecstack` declare, so those two are withheld and `pie`, `relro` and `textrel-absent` read over such a pair.

df_1_noopen.description: DF_1_NOOPEN in DT_FLAGS_1, the linker's record of `-z nodlopen`.

textrel.description: DF_TEXTREL in DT_FLAGS or a standalone DT_TEXTREL entry. Both spellings are read because bfd emits DT_FLAGS only when it is non-zero, so a reader of DT_FLAGS alone reads a text relocation recorded under the entry alone as absent.

dt_relr.description: A DT_RELR entry: relative relocations in the packed format.

dt_debug.description: A DT_DEBUG entry, the linker's mark of executable output; false on an object with no dynamic section. The third marker `static_pie` and `pie` accept beside DF_1_PIE and PT_INTERP: lld 10.0.0, measured on 2026-09-28, writes it on a static PIE it does not mark DF_1_PIE.

dt_soname.description: A DT_SONAME entry. Recorded and not consulted by the classification: a linker writes it for any output given -soname, so DT_DEBUG beside DT_SONAME is still executable output.

dynamic_tags.description: Every (tag, value) pair in the dynamic section, in file order, each as `0x<tag>=0x<value>` in lowercase hex. Carried so that a verdict which turns on one flag bit is auditable from the report alone, with no readelf against an artifact that may no longer exist. Empty when there is no dynamic section.

needed.description: Every DT_NEEDED string, resolved through the DT_STRTAB the dynamic section names, in dynamic-section order.

gnu_property_types.description: Every property type found in the object's NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0 notes, whatever the machine, ascending, each as `0x` and eight lowercase hex digits (`0xc0000002` is the x86 feature word, `0xc0000000` the aarch64 one). Only the five feature bits below are decoded from them, and only on the machine that defines the type.

gnu_property_notes.description: How many notes carried each type in `gnu_property_types`, keyed the same way. The linker merges its inputs into one note per output and its rule for a `*_FEATURE_1_AND` word is AND, so a linked object carries each type once; a count of two is a file no linker wrote, and the feature bits published for it are the AND of both notes. Present only when at least one property note exists.

x86_ibt.description: The IBT bit of GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an x86 object only; on any other machine the type is listed in `gnu_property_types` and no bit is read. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

x86_shstk.description: The SHSTK bit of GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an x86 object only; on any other machine the type is listed in `gnu_property_types` and no bit is read. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_bti.description: The BTI bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an aarch64 object only; on any other machine the type is listed in `gnu_property_types` and no bit is read. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_pac.description: The PAC bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an aarch64 object only; on any other machine the type is listed in `gnu_property_types` and no bit is read. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_gcs.description: The GCS bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an aarch64 object only; on any other machine the type is listed in `gnu_property_types` and no bit is read. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

openbsd_nobtcfi.description: The object carries a PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI program header (0x65a3dbe8, as OpenBSD 7.9 installs it in /usr/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/ELF.h), written by lld under `-z nobtcfi` for any target, OpenBSD's base linker and lld on Linux alike (GNU ld ignores the flag): the program's request that OpenBSD not enforce branch-target CFI on it, BTI on arm64 and IBT on amd64. Present only when true, so an absent member means the artifact carries no such request. `composites` reads it for `cfi-effective`.

sections.description: Section names as the name table stores them, in header order, with empty names dropped. Empty when the object has no section-header table or its name table could not be read, which `truncations` records.

data_in_code_pages.description: The allocated sections without SHF_EXECINSTR whose file bytes lie in a page an executable PT_LOAD maps, the page being that segment's p_align and never less than 4096 bytes, the smallest page a kernel for any machine the reader names maps, in header order; a section whose name could not be read is named by its index in brackets. `.note.gnu.build-id` is not counted, since Fedora's GNU ld places it in the code segment under `-z separate-code` on x86_64. Empty where the code pages hold code alone, which is what `-z separate-code` lays out. `null` where the question has no referent: no PT_LOAD carries PF_X, or no section header describes an allocated section. `ElfFacts` omits the member when `null`, and reads an absent member as `null`; an `elf` entry of a report's `facts` store states it. `separate-code` reads it.

code_relocations.description: On a relocatable object, the distinct relocations in sections whose target carries SHF_EXECINSTR, each as the type `readelf -r` names, one space and the symbol's name, sorted; a type the reader does not name is spelt `reloc-type-` and its number in hex. A relocation through a section symbol names the section in brackets in place of a symbol (`R_X86_64_PC32 [.data]`). A named symbol whose visibility is not STV_DEFAULT carries it as a third word (`R_386_PC32 __x86.get_pc_thunk.ax STV_HIDDEN`); a row of two words carries no visibility. Relocations patching data (debug sections, sanitizer descriptors), and those through symbol index 0 or an unnamed symbol of any other type, are left out. `null` for anything but an ET_REL with a section-header table. `ElfFacts` omits the member when `null`, and reads an absent member as `null`; an `elf` entry of a report's `facts` store states it. `plt-bypassed` and `pic-object-relocs` read it.

function_references.description: For a relocatable object, each defined STT_FUNC symbol in symbol-table order as `name:`, each followed by `name:target` for every distinct named symbol a relocation at an offset inside the function's range (`st_value` to `st_value + st_size` in its own section) refers to, the targets sorted and cut at their first `@`. After the functions, `?:target` for every distinct named symbol a relocation in code (a section with SHF_EXECINSTR) refers to from outside every function's range, sorted: the sections clang's `-fbasic-block-sections=all` holds a function's fragments in carry no function symbol. A function in a reserved section index is not listed. `null` where the object is not relocatable, has no SHT_SYMTAB, or is a 64-bit MIPS object, whose `r_info` the reader does not decode; a relocation section the reader could not finish is a `relocations` entry in `truncations`. `ElfFacts` omits the member when `null`, and reads an absent member as `null`; an `elf` entry of a report's `facts` store states it. `ssp-level-emitted` reads it.

symbol_tables.description: The symbol tables the file has, in header order: `.symtab` and `.dynsym` by name, or `SHT_SYMTAB` and `SHT_DYNSYM` where the section names could not be read. Absent when the object has none, which is the artifact precondition `canary-emitted`, `ssp-covers-small-arrays` and `cxx-assertions-symbol` read: a reference is read from `.symtab` or `.dynsym`, a stripped static link carries neither, and a reading over it is `not-applicable` under `artifact-cannot-carry-observable`. Symbol tables the reader could not reach are recorded in `truncations` instead, and `artifact-unreadable` speaks first.

symbol_count.description: Distinct symbol names across every symbol table read, keyed on the name before the first `@`, so a versioned and a bare spelling of one name count once.

watched_symbols.description: The symbols detectors ask about, keyed on the name before the first `@`, each present only when at least one table carried it. A name absent from the map was found in no table that was read; `truncations` says whether a table went unread.

table.description: The ELF table the reader could not finish, as `elf::ElfTable` spells it. `header` and `program-headers` are refused by `Elf::parse` and reach a report as a withheld observation, so no recorded entry names them; every other table has a recording site. `gnu-stack` names two PT_GNU_STACK headers within the program-header table that disagree on PF_X, recorded `unread`; the checks reading the stack header declare it beside `program-headers`. `section-headers` names a header escape whose `shdr[0]` the file does not hold: the cause, recorded beside the `symbols` and `section-names` entries it leads to, and declared by the checks whose predicates read section headers (`ret-protector-emitted` beside `section-names`, which the same escape records). `code` names a function `elf::code::SCANS` lists that the object defines and whose bytes could not be read whole, or a symbol-table entry the code reader could not read. `relocations` names a relocation section of a relocatable object that applies to code and could not be followed or read to its end, which `code_relocations` then lists in part and which withholds the checks declaring it, `ssp-level-emitted` among them.

kind.description: `unread`: the table's facts are absent because they could not be read, and a check declaring the table is withheld under the `artifact-unreadable` gating rule. `ignored`: a view of the table that disagreed with the loader's was dropped and the loader's view was measured, so the facts are whole and no check is withheld.

detail.description: The reader's own sentence, with the offset or index it stopped at; what a gating reason and a diagnostic quote.

truncations.description: Tables this parse could not read to their end, each typed by table and by what the cut did to the facts, so a consumer can tell a fact measured and absent from one that could not be read without matching prose. In a `facts` entry of kind `elf` it is always present, `[]` when every table was read whole, since a reader re-evaluating a predicate over the entry reads an absent list as not knowing rather than as nothing cut; an `elf-delta` states it where the arm's differs from its base's. Where `elf::ElfFacts` is serialized on its own (`chard elf`, the replay corpus, the synthetic fixtures) it is absent when every table was read whole.

comment.description: Distinct lines of the artifact's `.comment` section, in file order: each producer that touched the object appends its own (the compiler; lld and mold name themselves, GNU ld and gold write nothing). Absent when the section is missing or holds no line; a section that could not be read names itself in `truncations`.

function_entries.description: `<function>=<hex>` for each function `elf::entry::ENTRY_FUNCTIONS` names that the object defines in `.symtab` and whose bytes were read: its first four bytes (fewer where its `st_size` is smaller), as lowercase hex in file order, read at `st_value` through the section header `st_shndx` names. A listed function the object does not define contributes nothing; one defined and unreadable is in `truncations` under `function-entries`. `ElfFacts` omits the member when empty, and reads an absent member as empty; an `elf` entry of a report's `facts` store states it, `[]` included. `cet-endbr-emitted` reads it.

self_report.description: Contents of the `.chard.report` section: the artifact's own account of the macros in effect when it was compiled, self-reported and therefore cross-checked by the other channels: a `CHARD-REPORT-V2` line, one line per macro, `NAME=value` where it was defined and `NAME undefined` where it was not, and `CHARD-REPORT-END`. A `CHARD-REPORT-V1` header writes `NAME=?` for a macro not defined, which a macro defined as `?` also writes; chard reads that `?` as undefined. Empty when the section is absent.

recorded_command_line.description: Contents of `.GCC.command.line`, the literal driver command line when the toolchain was asked to record it (`-frecord-gcc-switches`, clang's `-frecord-command-line`). Explicit arguments only, so it complements the macro channel. Empty when the section is absent.

code_scanned.description: `<function>:<pattern>=<count>` for every pattern of the artifact's machine (`elf::code::CODE_PATTERNS`) that an `elf::code::SCANS` entry lists, searched in that entry's function where its bytes were read whole, zero counts included. A listed function the object does not define, or one whose list holds no pattern of the machine, contributes no entry, so the list says what was searched; a defined function that could not be read is in `truncations` under `code`. A fixed-pattern byte search over one function, not a disassembly. In a `facts` entry of kind `elf` it is always present, `[]` included, as `truncations` is; where `elf::ElfFacts` is serialized on its own it is absent when empty.

code_matches.description: `<function>:<pattern>@<offset>` for each match `code_scanned` counts, the offset from the function's first byte, at most `elf::code::MATCHES_KEPT` per function and pattern. Present in an `elf` entry, `[]` included, and absent when empty elsewhere, as `code_scanned` is.

controls.description: The self-validation triple. Without a discriminating control pair, an absent observable means nothing.

flags.description: What the arm was built with: exactly the check's declared positive control list, and no profile flag, since a control answers whether the detector can see the flag on this toolchain at all. Fixed when the triple is decided, so an arm cannot claim fewer flags than built it.

build.description: What the arm compiled, and what happened when it did. Published for every arm rather than retained only where the triple failed: an `off` rests on the negative arm having demonstrated absence, and a reader who doubts that needs the argv, the exit status and the artifact digest rather than a prose excerpt. Absent only where the arm was never built.

run.description: What the arm's artifact did when it was run. Absent on the macro, `elf-static` and `compiler-diag` channels, where no arm is executed, and on a runtime arm whose build failed.

outcome.description: Three-valued, and absent entirely when the arm could not be built or run. A boolean here would collapse `indeterminate` into `absent`, and a negative arm demonstrating absence is exactly what licenses an `off` verdict.

detail.description: What the detector actually observed for this arm, except that paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary object names read `<compiler-temp>`. A quoted stream inside it is cut to a budget, and a cut is never silent: `[N chars omitted]`, counted in characters, stands on each cut side in place of what was removed. On the compiler-diag channel the part kept is the line the detector matched and the lines around it, so the diagnostic the arm's outcome rests on is always quoted; on the other channels it is the stream's end, where a libc message or the probe's own reading lands. When `outcome` is absent, the arm could not be evaluated and this names why: the `-dM -E` dump that failed, with its exit status and first stderr line; the run that could not be spawned; or the build that failed. Present so a reader can check the discrimination claim rather than taking it on trust.
