A quoted stream inside it is cut to a budget, and a cut is never silent: `[N chars omitted]`, counted in characters, stands on each cut side in place of what was removed. On the compiler-diag channel the part kept is the line the detector matched and the lines around it, so the diagnostic the arm's outcome rests on is always quoted; on the other channels it is the stream's end, where a libc message or the probe's own reading lands. When `outcome` is absent, the arm could not be evaluated and this names why: the `-dM -E` dump that failed, with its exit status and first stderr line; the run that could not be spawned; or the build that failed. Present so a reader can check the discrimination claim rather than taking it on trust.

macro_source.description: Where the arm's macros were read from, on every arm of a macro-channel check and on no other: `compiled-artifact` for the arm artifact's own `.chard.report`, in the `facts` entry under `build.artifact_sha256`; `preprocessor` for its `cc -dM -E` dump, in the `macro-dump` entry under `macro_dump.stdout_sha256`.

macro_dump.description: The arm's own `cc -dM -E` job, on every arm of a macro-channel check, with its defines replaced by a count as on `evidence.macro_dump` and their digest kept as `stdout_sha256`. A `positive-unevaluable` or `negative-unevaluable` on the macro channel was withheld by this job, and its exit status and stderr are the only account of it.

decoded.description: The predicate's reading of this arm, on every arm with an `outcome` of a macro or `elf-static` check; its `outcome` is the arm's.

regime_negative.description: The negative control re-run in the measured profile's own regime. The profile-free arms show the detector can see the flag at all; they cannot show that the signal in the measured build is attributable to it, because they ran under different optimization and hardening settings. When this arm shows the observable, the verdict is withheld: a co-enabled flag is producing the signal.

discriminating.description: positive showed the observable AND negative did not. When false the measurement verdict must be `probe-invalid`.

withheld_because.description: Why the triple licensed no verdict, as a closed set beside the sentence in `failure_reason`. Present exactly when `discriminating` is false: the two are serialized from one value, so a report cannot claim discrimination and name a failure at the same time. A set rather than prose because the withheld checks are a queue somebody has to work through, and a queue that can only be counted by reading English is one nobody counts.

check.description: Check id within the probe. A probe may carry several checks, so this is the unit a verdict attaches to.

flag.description: Canonical flag this probe reports on, e.g. -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE.

polarity.description: harden: presence is good. weaken: presence is bad (an RPATH or RUNPATH entry, a text relocation) and `off` is the protected state, so a renderer can colour cells without flag knowledge.

level.description: The level the detector reported, as a word on the check's own vocabulary, which `chard probes` publishes per check under `levels`: a number for _FORTIFY_SOURCE, "basic"/"strong"/"all" for ssp (and, for ssp-level-emitted alone, "unsafe-frame", a word the scale admits on no rung, listed under `levels.ungraded`: clang's SafeStack placing a canary in exactly the functions it gave an unsafe frame, published as the level with verdict `on` and graded against nothing), "partial"/"full" for RELRO, "branch"/"return"/"full" for the control-flow components. Graded against `recommended_level` where that key is present and published as information where it is absent. Present only beside a measurement verdict: a word the check's scale cannot grade withholds the verdict as `indeterminate` under `gating.rule: level-outside-check-scale`, and the word then survives in `gating.reason` and `evidence.observed` only. ABSENT when no level was established — never null. A missing key makes an `== expected` policy test fail closed, where an explicit null passes the `!= bad` idiom that much real policy is written in.

recommended_level.description: What the OpenSSF guide recommends, on the check's own scale, enabling a `partial` verdict to be computed rather than hardcoded. Present exactly where the check grades a level; absent where the check grades nothing and any `level` is information (`pie`, `pie-macro`, `cxx-hardening-requested`, the diagnostic-presence checks) — never null.

confidence.description: How directly the check's observable establishes the protection, fixed when the check is written rather than varying per run. Not a probability, and not a restatement of `channel` or of `controls.discriminating`: `compiler-diag` checks split across both values, and `discriminating` varies with the run while this does not.

observable.description: Human-readable statement of what was looked at.

boundary.description: Where this verdict stops. Every verdict here is a property of the artifact — what the binary opts into — and some protections only take effect if the kernel, the CPU or the C library also cooperate, none of which a measurement of a file can establish. Present only for protections with such a dependency: a stack canary, a fortified call and full RELRO need nothing further, so those observations carry no boundary and absence means `nothing outside this file is required` rather than `not considered`.

establishes.description: What the verdict does establish, in the artifact.

requires_at_runtime.description: What must also hold where the binary runs, and which this report does not check.

defects.description: Ids of the defect classes this check's flag bears on. Authored by this project, not cited: the OpenSSF guide names mechanisms in prose and cites no CWE anywhere. Empty is meaningful — it says the flag is not a mitigation.

observes.description: What this check's `on` is evidence of toward `defects`. protection: the mechanism itself, in the artifact or at run time, or its producer's own word for its state (`__SSP_STRONG__`, `__USE_FORTIFY_LEVEL`). request: a macro the build supplied to ask for it (`_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`, `_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE`). marking: a property note, landing pad or compiler macro for a control-flow mechanism a CPU enforces (CET, BTI, PAC, GCS), whose enforcement the check does not observe. `defect_coverage` moves a status on protection alone; a request or marking is tallied under `requested`, `marked`, `not-requested` or `not-marked` and moves it in neither direction. The bearing table's word: for a report of this corpus (`run.probe_corpus_sha256` this binary's, which folds the field in) the value is held to the table on read. Required of what `measure` writes. On read, a report without it is refused whatever its corpus. A report of another corpus with it on none of its observations is refused as a report shape this chard does not write, one whose rollup counts every bearing check as protection. A request stays one where a library's own default defines the macro (libstdc++'s `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` at -O0).

evidence.description: Channel-specific raw evidence, small but sufficient to re-derive the verdict without re-running. Exactly the members the code can emit are declared and any other is refused, so a renamed or added member fails validation on the first host that emits it. An observation withheld by the applicability gate that runs before any channel is read carries `{}` and names its rule in `gating`; one withheld because its variant could not serve the channel carries `observed` with the reason where one was recorded, plus `macro_source` and `macro_dump` on the macro channel. An observation's ELF facts are the `facts` entry under its `build.artifact_sha256`, not this block.

macros_filter.description: SHA-256 of the name list `macros` was trimmed to, which `evidence_filters.macros` carries in full. Present exactly when `macros` is: the map beside it is a filtered view, and this is the pointer to the filter.

macro_source.description: Where `macros` was read from: the probe's own `.chard.report` section, or the `cc -dM -E` dump when the artifact carried none. Present on macro-channel observations only.

macro_dump.description: The `cc -dM -E` job's own record, on every macro-channel observation, with its defines replaced by a count of them (see `build_record.stdout`). Its exit status and its output gate the channel: a dump that exited non-zero withholds every verdict read through it, whatever it printed first, and so do one that exited 0 and defined nothing and one that exited 0 with its output cut off partway through a line (`stdout_unterminated`), on every host; the probe's own `.chard.report` rescues none of them. `observed` names the status and the first line of stderr, the cut, or the emptiness.

observed.description: What the detector saw, in one line, or why the channel could not be read when the verdict was withheld before any detector ran.

decoded.description: The predicate's reading of the measured build, on every observation of a macro or `elf-static` check that reached its decoder. An ungated `on`, `off` or `partial` is the verdict this reading gives on the check's scale: `absent` is `off`, `present` is `on`, or on a graded check `on` or `partial` by the level.

cxx_assertions_source.description: What put libstdc++'s assertions into the measured build, on `cxx-hardening-requested`, `cxx-stdlib-assertions` and `cxx-assertions-symbol`: `profile` where the profile's C++ flags leave `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` or `_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` defined (the `-Wp,` and `-Xpreprocessor` forms applied after the plain ones, the last word winning within each); `library-unoptimized-default` where their `-D` and `-U` spellings leave neither defined, the build has no `__OPTIMIZE__`, and they leave `_GLIBCXX_NO_ASSERTIONS` undefined, the condition under which `c++config.h` defines the assertions itself, and the flags carry no `-include`, `-imacros`, `-include-pch`, `@file` or `-Xclang -D`/`-U` argument, whose content the attribution does not read (gcc's long spellings of `-D` and `-U`, `--define-macro` and `--def`, are read as them); `unattributed` where neither holds: the profile's `-D` and `-U` flags do not account for the assertions, and either the library's unoptimized condition does not hold or the profile carries one of those unread arguments, so chard names no source. The source may be such an argument on the profile's own flag line, a driver default or a spec file. Read from the measured build's macros as published: `macros` on the macro channel, the `.chard.report` of the build's `facts` entry elsewhere. Absent where `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` is undefined, the library is not libstdc++, or the observation built no control triple. The verdicts do not depend on it: an `on` over the library's default is true of the artifact.

gating.description: Why a check was `unsupported`, `not-applicable`, or withheld as `indeterminate` by a named rule rather than `off`. Each rule's premise fixes the one verdict it publishes, and the consistency rule `gating-rule-reserves-a-different-verdict` refuses a report where the two disagree. A fact about the measured system (its toolchain, target, C library or kernel) publishes `unsupported`: `arch-gated`, `libc-declared`, `compiler-declared`, `flag-unknown-to-driver`, `flag-refused-by-driver`, `linker-keyword-ignored`, `fortify-level-declined`, `link-drops-marking`, `subobject-bound-lost-in-wrapper`, `kernel-lacks-shadow-stack`. A limit of chard's instrument publishes `indeterminate`: `needs-vm`, `execution-mode-assumed`, `no-check-on-target`, `arch-outside-table`, `unhardened-state-unbuildable`, `scaffolding-unbuildable`, `macro-supplied-by-profile`, `no-driver`, `probe-unmeasured`, `artifact-unreadable`, `artifact-holds-lto-ir`, `artifact-lacks-self-report`, `artifact-contradicts-link-mode`, `level-outside-check-scale`, `guard-kept-without-the-flag`, `run-output-unreadable`, `run-deadline-elapsed`, `run-under-emulation`, `target-arch-contradicted`, `target-abi-contradicted`, `cpu-lacks-shadow-stack`, `opt-in-not-honoured`, `loader-refuses-execstack`, `link-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`, `clean-link-unmatched-by-measured`, `compile-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`, `sanitizer-group-unmeasured`, `lto-codegen-at-link`, `macro-contradicted-by-artifact`. A question with no referent in what was measured publishes `not-applicable`: `artifact-cannot-carry-observable`, `stdlib-lacks-observable`. `premise` names the rule's class beside its id, as the table of the chard that wrote the report has it, and a reader sorts the observation by that class rather than by its own table, so a report keeps the standing its writer gave it; where the reading chard's table has the rule under another class, or has no such rule, `table` and `matrix` say so in a note and refuse nothing for the difference alone, unless the report's `run.harness_revision` is the reader's own clean revision, whose table is the one that wrote it. The class is the file's word, and so is the revision: an editor who changes both is read under the class written. `chard digest` refuses the same-revision case as `table` does and otherwise prints the report's own digest with no note.

needs_vm.description: Verdict depends on the kernel; withheld under `needs-vm` where environment.execution.mode is container, and under `execution-mode-assumed` where it is host on an `assumed-host` basis.

premise.description: The class of `rule`'s premise in the table of the chard that wrote the report, which fixes the one verdict the observation carries: `toolchain-fact` publishes `unsupported`, `instrument-limitation` publishes `indeterminate`, and `inapplicable` publishes `not-applicable`. Where it is absent, the reader takes the class from its own table. `coverage.withholding` counts the observation as an earned limitation exactly when its verdict is the one this class publishes and is `unsupported` or `not-applicable`, and `gating-rule-reserves-a-different-verdict` refuses, at publication and on read, a verdict this class does not publish.

rule.description: Which rule withheld the check, beside the sentence in `reason`. A gating is otherwise distinguishable only by its prose, so a question as ordinary as `how often does a declared libc limitation explain a silence` would need a regular expression over English to answer. `artifact-unreadable` is the reader's own statement about the measured artifact: a table the check's observable is read from could not be finished, so the reading is withheld as `indeterminate`; a `probe-invalid` the triple produced carries no gating, since its controls carry the cause, and a control arm cut the same way withholds through `controls.withheld_because`. `artifact-holds-lto-ir` withholds an elf-static reading, whatever it was and unless the check's observable was measured to survive into such an object (`cet-marked-object`), over a measured object that holds `.gnu.lto_*` sections beside gcc's `__gnu_lto_slim` marker, or beside a symbol table the reader could not finish: a slim LTO object carries compiler IR and no generated code, so the observable is produced at the final link the probe does not perform; it withholds a macro-channel reading over such an object too where the object defines the marker and its section list holds no `.chard.report`, whose self-report is then in the IR. `artifact-lacks-self-report` withholds a macro-channel reading, whatever it was short of `probe-invalid` and `unsupported`, over a measured build whose artifact gave no account of its macros: the artifact's `.chard.report` is not in `elf.sections`, or is listed and the reader could not finish it (an `elf.truncations` entry naming it), or nothing was reached by section name (no section-header table, or a name table the reader refused), or the section is listed and holds no report (the `CHARD-REPORT-V2` marker, or a `CHARD-REPORT-V1` header, `CHARD-REPORT-END` after it and at least one field between them; a field `name undefined`, or `name=?` under V1, is the artifact's word that the macro is undefined, under V2 `name=?` is a macro defined as `?`, and a report whose fields all read undefined is an account the channel reads, as an empty map), or holds a report the reader cannot read whole (a `CHARD-REPORT-V2` report with a line that is neither `name=value` nor `name undefined`, a blank line, a name given twice or a second marker, or a `CHARD-REPORT-V1` report with a second marker: a line dropped would read as a macro undefined); or the build exited 0 and wrote none (on every host: there is nothing to read on any), or the reader refused the artifact (the `unreadable` entry under its digest), unless it refused a Mach-O object (`mach_o`) on a macOS run. The macro channel's witness is that section, written by the same compiler invocation that generated the code; where the artifact gives no account, `measure` leaves the `-dM -E` dump as `macros` (`evidence.macro_source` `preprocessor`), a witness no artifact channel can hold to the generated code, and this rule withholds the reading rather than publish it. The control arms stay dump readings and may discriminate, so the gate is on the measured build and a `probe-invalid` keeps its controls' cause; an arm that lost its section says so in its own `macro_source`. A macOS run reads the dump by design over a Mach-O object the reader refused and is not gated there; every other refusal is gated on every host. The reason names the way the artifact gave no account and quotes the reader's entry or refusal where there is one. The consistency rule `macro-verdict-unearned-by-artifact` refuses a report that publishes a macro-channel measurement over such a build. `artifact-contradicts-link-mode` withholds a reading of `pie`, or of `as-needed` where it read the classification (no `DT_NEEDED` entry naming the C library, or the C library recorded and the unused library not), on the measured build as `indeterminate`: it is keyed on the classification fields the reading rested on, so `as-needed` over a list that recorded the unused library, which it read without the classification, stands. It fires where the probe asked the driver for an executable and its artifact classifies as a shared object (`elf.shared_object`): an `ET_DYN` with a dynamic section, no interpreter, and neither `DF_1_PIE` nor `DT_DEBUG`. Those tags are a static PIE written with neither marker (lld 10.0.0 under clang 10 `-static-pie -Wl,-z,rodynamic`, Ubuntu 20.04 x86_64), or output a link flag such as a profile's `-shared` turned into a shared object, and the tags do not say which. chard adds `-shared` or `-c` to `build.argv` for the other link modes and nothing for an executable, so a `-shared` there under this rule is the profile's. The reason names the classification fields the reading rests on. `run-output-unreadable` is the same statement about a runtime check's run: a stream reached the capture cap or could not be read, so a marker absent from it is chard's silence, and the reading is withheld whatever it was. `run-deadline-elapsed` withholds a runtime reading, whatever it was, whose probe was killed at `run.deadlines.probe_run_ms` (`timed_out` with `signal` `SIGKILL` or no status), since a killed probe never finished writing; the reason quotes the deadline. `run-under-emulation` withholds a runtime reading, whatever it was, of a check whose reading rests on the machine (`run_basis` `machine` in `chard probes`: `stack-clash-guard-page`, and `shadow-stack-enforced`) when the measured artifact's `elf.machine`, `elf_class` and `elf_data` are not ones the kernel executes natively (`environment.kernel.machine`, or `environment.kernel.arch` where that is absent; the kernel's byte order from its spelling, `env::kernel_byte_order`), so a `binfmt_misc` interpreter, an emulator such as qemu-user, produced the reading, or where the record carries no byte order or the kernel's spelling names none, or where the artifact's entry in `facts` is `unreadable` (a Mach-O program on Darwin), so nothing holds it to the kernel, except on a macOS run (`environment.distro.id` `macos`) whose measured run's `stdout` carries the probe's `CHARD-TRANSLATION 0`, its read of `sysctl.proc_translated`, which publishes the reading; there a `1` (Rosetta 2 translated the run), an unreadable read, no such line, a line in no shape chard reads, or the marker on any line but the first withhold; the reason quotes both machines, or the reader's refusal and what the probe read. `kernel-lacks-shadow-stack` and `cpu-lacks-shadow-stack` name `shadow-stack-enforced` where its positive control read `indeterminate` and that arm's own run, executed natively, says the machine cannot run a shadow stack. `kernel-lacks-shadow-stack` publishes `unsupported` where the kernel answered `arch_prctl(ARCH_SHSTK_STATUS)` with `EINVAL`: the kernel is the measured system's own. `cpu-lacks-shadow-stack` withholds as `indeterminate` where the kernel offers the interface and the CPU does not enumerate CET shadow stack in CPUID leaf 7: the CPU is the one chard's run was handed, in a VM the hypervisor's virtual CPU, and not the distribution's. Each reason quotes the run's `SHSTK` line. `link-inputs-unmatched-by-arms` withholds, whatever the triple concluded, a check whose observable the link's startup objects decide (`cet-marked`, `branch-protection-marked`, `gcs-marked`, `noexecstack`, `noexecstack-enforced`, `shadow-stack-enforced`, `textrel-absent`) where the driver's `-###` names another link program, other inputs (startup objects, archives or any other file, whatever its name), library directories or system root for the measured build's link than for the control arms' selection under the same linkage form, or where either listing could not be read: a gcc `-specs=` or clang `--config=` file reaches the measured build and not the arms, and can choose the startup objects. The reason quotes the paths on each side. `clean-link-unmatched-by-measured` withholds, whatever the triple concluded, a check that reads the clean build (`linker-default-noexecstack`) where the driver names another link program, library directory, system root or search directory for that build than for the measured build: the program, the `-L` directories and the system root from the `-###` link line of the clean build's flags with the measured line's linker program selection (`-fuse-ld=`, `--ld-path=`) against the measured build's, the program and library lists from `-print-search-dirs` under the clean build's own flags against the measured build's; or where any of the four answers could not be read, which includes a `-print-search-dirs` answer that lacks either list. The clean build carries the profile's target and runtime selection as chard read it from the flags, so a word chard reads otherwise than the driver (a `-B` or `-L` taken as the profile's own where the driver took it as an option's value) can hand the clean build alone another linker or library. The reason quotes what each side names, or the answer that could not be read. `compile-inputs-unmatched-by-arms` withholds in the same way a check whose observable the compile's headers or predefined macros decide (every macro-channel check, `fortify-printf-flag`, `fortify-enforced-known`, `fortify-enforced-dynamic`, `fortify-level-ge-2-subobject`, `fortify-level-ge-2-percent-n`, `strict-flex-arrays-enforced`, `cxx-stdlib-assertions` and `cxx-assertions-symbol`) where the driver's `-###` under `-no-integrated-cpp` names other compile programs, targets, header search directories, system root, forced includes, `-D` or `-U` operations or removed defaults for the measured build's compile than for the arms' selection with the profile's own optimisation, `-D` and `-U` words (the optimisation words so that a macro the driver adds by itself under `-O`, as Ubuntu's gcc adds `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, reaches both listings; a listing at each other level the arms carry is compared with it too, and a difference there other than in a macro the controls set withholds the checks at that level), or where either listing could not be read: a specs `*cpp` or `*cc1` and a configuration file's `--gcc-install-dir=` reach the measured compile and not the arms. The reason quotes what each side names. `lto-codegen-at-link` withholds an `on` of `pic-shared-link` under a driver that is not gcc where the measured compile's `-###` command leaves link-time optimization in effect (clang's `-cc1` carries the resolved `-flto=full` or `-flto=thin`, a configuration file's included), or where that listing could not be read: the link generates the code from bitcode and chooses its position-independence, so a `-shared` link that succeeds does not show the profile's flags made the code position-independent. An `off` is left standing. The reason quotes the compile's LTO words and its code-model words. The rule does not fire (and the `on` stands, with the `-cc1` words quoted in `evidence.observed`) where that command resolves the compile to `-fPIC` or `-fpic` without PIE: `-mrelocation-model pic`, a `-pic-level` of 1 or 2, and no `-pic-is-pie`. `no-check-on-target` and `arch-outside-table` are the mechanism table's two withholdings at applicability, beside `arch-gated`, which the table decides too: `arch-gated` is published only where the target answers the check's question with another mechanism a check reads, so its statement holds; `no-check-on-target` where the target has a mechanism for the question, the check's own with no construction for the target or another no check reads, the reason quoting the row's witness; `arch-outside-table` where the table has no row for the target. Neither of the two sets `gating.arch`, and both count the check among `coverage.withholding.instrument_withholdings`, as `needs-vm` does. `target-abi-contradicted` withholds, after every probe is measured, an arch-gated check decided under a read architecture the table has a row for, whatever it had, where `toolchain.target.abi` reads `disagrees`: an artifact of the read family, or a dump that agreed about the family, carries a width or byte order other than the one the architecture's rows stand for (an x32 or aarch64 ILP32 object, an aarch64_be dump), so the target is one the table has no row for; a check `target-arch-contradicted` withheld keeps that rule. The reason quotes the verdict it had, the decision the gate took, what the rows stand for and the witness. `execution-mode-assumed` withholds, at applicability and before any build, a check that declares `needs_vm` where `environment.execution.mode` is `host` on an `assumed-host` basis: nothing observed the mode and nobody asserted it, and a container chard has no instrument for (systemd-nspawn, LXC without a cgroup needle, Apptainer, mock, a chroot) reads the same as a bare host or a VM guest, so whose kernel policy the reading would describe is unsettled; `needs-vm` withholds the same checks under `container`, and the operator's `--execution host` or `vm`, recorded as `asserted-but-unobservable`, publishes them. The reason quotes `mode_evidence.observation`. Like `needs-vm`, it sets `needs_vm` and counts the check among `coverage.withholding.instrument_withholdings`. `macro-supplied-by-profile`: the profile's flag list defines or undefines, in a spelling the rule reads, a macro the compiler defines to describe its own code generation and this check reads, or a macro the check's probe branches on in its own source (`measure::PROBE_MACRO_BRANCHES`), or carries a preprocessor input the rule does not read by name beside such a probe, or selects a header search directory beside such a probe's compile-input readings, or carries such an input or selects a header search directory beside a macro check with no artifact or runtime twin (`report::MACRO_WITHOUT_TWIN`: `optimization-enabled`, `fortify-effective`); the reading is of the list, withheld as `indeterminate`. `macro-contradicted-by-artifact`: a macro-channel reading of a code-generation observable whose twin, a check reading the same protection from the artifact or a run of it (`report::MACRO_TWINS`), read the opposite presence in the same report; the macro reading is withheld as `indeterminate` with the reason naming both readings, and the twin keeps its verdict. Consulted after `target-arch-contradicted` over the settled verdicts, so it overwrites no earlier gating; a twin that is withheld or absent from the run decides nothing, and a macro reading at an opt-in level is held to nothing. `guard-kept-without-the-flag` withholds, as `indeterminate`, a `no-strict-overflow` reading whose probe's guard ran and whose survival this build cannot attribute to the flag: the compiler keeps the guard at the measured build's optimization level without the flag (clang, and gcc before 8, at -O0; gcc before 8 at -O, -O1 and -Og) or is not one chard knows to fold it there (a compiler the probe names as neither gcc nor clang), the level or the gcc version that decides its reading cannot be read from the build (no `-O` word, `-O0` last beside an optimized run, a level not measured, a specs file, prefix directory, forced include, plugin or wrapper on the line, no build record, no readable `gcc-major=`), or something printed on stderr, as a sanitizer's checked add does, which keeps the guard whether or not the flag was passed. The reason is the detector's own sentence, `evidence.observed`, which says which. The detector names the rule in its reading, and `measure::settle` publishes it where the triple discriminated, after `level-outside-check-scale` and before the run and artifact gates, which overwrite it; `coverage.withholding` counts the observation under `by_rule`, not under `no_named_cause`.

structured_diagnostics.description: Present only under `--structured-diagnostics`, on a compiler-diag check the structured decoder has needles for. Each built arm is rebuilt with the compiler's SARIF on stderr and both decoders are asked the check's one question: the severity of the first diagnostic carrying one of its needles. The verdict is the prose decoder's either way; this is evidence about the decoder, not the toolchain.

format.description: The flag the side build carried: `-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr` for gcc, `-fdiagnostics-format=sarif` for clang, the only structured forms measured on gcc 16.1.1 / 16.2.1 and clang 22.1.8 (Fedora 44, 2026-09-28).

arms_expected.description: How many arms the comparison was fed: 3, the measured build and both controls, the negative being the clean build where the check has no negative control. `arms` and `arms_missing` together account for every one.

arms_missing.description: Arms fed with no build of their own or no side build, so nothing was compared. Each is also a warning in `diagnostics`. Absent when empty.

arms.description: Keyed by `measured`, `positive`, `negative`. An arm with no build or no side build is absent here and named in `arms_missing`.

structured.description: `note` is kept rather than folded into `warning`, where the prose decoder reads a matched line with no severity word as a warning.

reason.description: Why the side build's stream could not be decoded.

build_rejection.description: Present on `build-failed` when the toolchain rejected flags the *profile* supplied, so the failure is not about this check. Two independent signals must agree: the tool said it did not recognise something, and a token on that line is a flag chard passed from the profile. Measured on Darwin under openssf-tldr, where Apple's ld rejects -z, --as-needed and --no-copy-dt-needed-entries in one line and 23 of 51 checks fail to link for it. The sibling of the elf_error handling at the build step rather than the read step: an existing verdict plus a reason, not a ninth verdict. It names the build's first refusal line; a build that refused further profile flags on later lines is counted under each of them by the `profile-flag-rejected` diagnostics.

cwe.description: Attached only where one maps unambiguously; several of these mechanisms have no clean CWE and inventing one would be worse than leaving it absent.

fires_at_level.description: The effective _FORTIFY_SOURCE level at which this rung begins to fire.

reference.description: A link to where a flag was argued about. Universal references only — anything tied to one distribution belongs in a claim, which is filtered per report.

claim.description: What a published source claims about a flag on a distribution. Carried so a measurement can be compared against it: a stale wiki page and a real regression look identical until somebody checks.

distro.description: os-release id, or `*` when not distribution-specific.

since.description: Release the source says it applies from; later releases are covered.

mechanism.description: Where the source says it comes from: compiler or build-system.

agrees.description: Absent when there is nothing to compare — a withheld verdict is not evidence against a claim, and a claim about another release is not a claim about this one.

tables.description: ELF tables whose unread truncation concludes indeterminate under the clause @truncated.

clauses.description: Tried in order; the first whose condition holds concludes.

id.description: Unique within the predicate; never empty and never beginning with @, which the reserved clauses use.

because.description: The reason the clause concludes; it holds a character outside ECMA-262's \s.

elf_field.description: The ElfFacts keys a predicate may read, as $defs/elf_facts in chard-report.schema.json spells them.

decoded.description: One predicate reading as a value, on the measured build of every macro and `elf-static` observation that reached its decoder (`evidence.decoded`) and on every control arm with an `outcome` (`controls.*.decoded`), whether or not the triple discriminated. The reads are not published: a reader recomputes them by evaluating `decoders.predicates[check]` with the Published view of `src/predicate/mod.rs` over the `facts` entries named here, the macro filter `evidence_filters.macros` where the macro map is a `macro-dump`, and the watch list `evidence_filters.symbols`, and `decoded-reading-disagrees-with-facts` does exactly that for every reading.

facts.description: The `facts` key the reading's own channel was read from: the artifact digest on the `elf-static` channel; on the macro channel the key of the macro map, the artifact digest under `macro_source: compiled-artifact` (its `.chard.report`) or the dump's `stdout_sha256` under `preprocessor` (a `macro-dump` entry).

macros.description: The `facts` key of the macro map an `elf-static` predicate that reads macros was evaluated over, keyed as `facts` is on the macro channel. Absent on the macro channel and on a predicate that reads no macro.

clause.description: The deciding clause's id, or one of the reserved clauses `@no-source:macros`, `@no-source:elf`, `@truncated` and `@otherwise`.

level.description: The conclusion's level, where it has one.

withholding_set.description: One of `coverage.withholding`'s two sets. Each member is counted once by verdict and once by reason: `by_verdict` sums to `count`, and `by_rule`, `by_withheld_cause` and `no_named_cause` sum to `count` between them.

by_verdict.description: The set's observations by verdict. Absent when the set is empty.

by_rule.description: The set's observations carrying a `gating.rule`, by the rule's id. Absent when none does.

by_withheld_cause.description: The set's observations carrying no gating rule whose control triple withheld (not the removed top-level field of this name, which counted every failed triple), by `controls.withheld_because`. A rule, where one is carried, names the cause more closely than the triple (`cpu-lacks-shadow-stack` beside `positive-indeterminate`), so an observation carrying both is counted under its rule alone. Absent when none is counted here.

no_named_cause.description: The set's observations carrying neither a gating rule nor a triple's cause: an `indeterminate` a discriminating triple reached, whose `evidence.observed` says why, or a `build-failed` or `run-failed`, whose build or run record does. Always 0 in `earned_limitations`, whose every member is counted under its rule.

digest.description: The report's verdicts and what they stand on, ahead of the evidence: the first key of every report, and what `chard digest` prints alone. Derived from the report's own fields and nothing else, and held to them by the `digest-disagrees-with-report` consistency rule when `table`, `matrix` or `digest` reads the report; it carries no notes, references, facts, decoders, invocation or score. `coverage.verdict_counts` and `coverage.withholding` are recounted from `observations`; the rest is copied from the field each member names. A report without a digest does not validate against this schema; `table` and `matrix` still read it, and `chard digest` refuses it.

chard_schema.description: The report's `chard_schema`, so the block printed alone names its shape.

consistency.description: The report's `consistency.status`, the word `measure` wrote after applying every rule `rules_applied` names; reading the report, chard re-runs only the rules that need nothing outside the file. A published report reads `consistent`; `contradicted` is found only in a report `measure` refused and kept as `<file>.contradicted`, which `chard digest` refuses.

verdict_counts.description: The observations' verdicts, counted as published, whatever the polarity: a `weaken` check's `off` (the flag's effect absent) is its protected state and is counted under `off` with the rest.

checks.description: One row per observation, in the report's order.

level.description: `observations[].level`, absent where the observation carries none.

polarity.description: `observations[].polarity`. For a `weaken` check `off` is the protected state: the flag's effect is absent.

gating.description: `observations[].gating.rule`, where a gating rule decided the verdict.

reasons.description: One entry per observation that is not a measurement (neither `on`, `off` nor `partial`), in the report's order: every reason the report gives in one place. Absent when every check measured.

standing.description: Which of `coverage.withholding`'s two sets the observation is counted in: `earned-limitation` for an `unsupported` or `not-applicable` beside a `gating.rule` whose premise publishes that verdict, `instrument-withholding` for every other.

reason.description: The report's sentence for it, whitespace folded to single spaces: a `build-failed`'s `build_rejection`, else `gating.reason`, else `controls.failure_reason` where the triple withheld, else `evidence.observed`, a blank one passed over. Absent where the observation carries none of them.

meaning.description: What a column under the profile measures against what a distribution's package build injects: one sentence per `profile.flags_source`, with a clause where `toolchain.config_files` names a file (the `driver-config-file` sentence names it already) and one where `profile.id` carries the `+env:` suffix of `--env` pairs.

harness_revision.description: `run.harness_revision`, absent where the report carries none.

harness_revision_source.description: `run.harness_revision_source`, absent where the report carries none.

harness_rustflags_sha256.description: `run.harness_rustflags_sha256`, absent where the report carries none.

withholding.description: What this report measured, what it established as a limitation, and what chard withheld: three counts that add to `checks_attempted`. Each observation that is not a measurement is in exactly one of the two sets, sorted by its verdict and the id of its `gating.rule`. Derivable from the observations, which is why it exists: deriving it needs the verdict vocabulary and the gating rules' premises, and a reader without them sees a table of clean-looking cells. No rate is published, because the counts are the statement and a rate over either set reads as a grade of the toolchain. Held to `verdict_counts` and to the observations by the `withholding-disagrees-with-verdict-counts` rule, when the report is written and when `table` or `matrix` reads it. A block with `withheld` and no `earned_limitations` counts the two sets together, beside `percent_withheld`, `by_verdict` and `by_withheld_cause` at its top level; it is not comparable with this one, and `table` and `matrix` refuse it and name it. The `by_verdict` and `by_withheld_cause` inside each set are not those top-level fields: each counts that set's members alone, and a set's `by_withheld_cause` counts only the members carrying no gating rule.

published.description: Observations carrying on, off or partial.

earned_limitations.description: Answers that are not measurements: each observation carrying `unsupported` or `not-applicable` beside a `gating.rule` whose premise publishes that verdict, so the measured system lacks the mechanism (its toolchain, target, C library or kernel, as the rule says), or the question has no referent in what was measured. They settle `all_verdicts_published`.

instrument_withholdings.description: Checks that earned no verdict: chard could not pose or read the question, or the build or run it needed failed (a profile flag the toolchain rejects is named in `diagnostics`). Every other observation that is not a measurement, which is each `probe-invalid`, `indeterminate`, `build-failed` and `run-failed`, and an `unsupported` or `not-applicable` no gating rule earns. Empty exactly when every attempted check is settled, and each member is one line of a failed `--fail-on-missing`, beside a line for each corpus check not attempted, which is in neither set.
